DEATH PROBE Tragedy as man found dead inside vehicle in Morrisons car park

A MAN has tragically been found dead in a car outside a Morrisons.

Officers cordoned off the store’s car park car park in Bolton, Greater Manchester, following the grim discovery yesterday morning.



Greater Manchester Police confirmed it was called out after receiving reports of concerns for a man’s welfare.

The force said: “At around 9.40am on September 9, officers received a call regarding a concern for the welfare of a man on Blackhorse Street, Bolton.



“Sadly, a man was found dead in a car. There are not believed to be any suspicious circumstances.”

News.title: Man hit by car & teen dragged along road after driver ploughs into them during road rage row sparked by crash
News.content:
ROAD RAGE PROBE Man hit by car & teen dragged along road after driver ploughs into them during road rage row sparked by crash

A DRIVER left a man with life-changing injuries then dragged a teenager along the road after a road rage row, cops have said.

The man in his 50s was involved in an argument with the two men in Salford following the crash at 5.40pm on Wednesday.

After being confronted, he sped away and struck one of the men who challenged him, who was taken to hospital with life-changing injuries.



An 18-year-old who also confronted the driver was injured when he was dragged along with the vehicle as it fled the scene, Greater Manchester Police said.



The teenager remains in hospital with non-life threatening or changing injuries.

A man has been arrested on suspicion of grievous bodily harm with intent and remains in custody. Investigations are ongoing.

Police have urged any witnesses or people with dashcam, CCTV or mobile footage to get in touch by calling 101, quoting log 2694 of 09/09/26.

A police spokesman said: “At around 5.40pm last night (September 9), we were called to reports of a hit and run on Broughton Lane in Salford.

“It was established that there had been a road traffic collision where two people from one of the vehicles have got out to challenge the driver of the other car following the collision.

“Upon doing so, the driver has proceeded to make off and struck one of the two men – a man in his 50s – who was taken to hospital and remains there with life-changing injuries.



“The second man – an 18-year-old man – also received an injury during the incident, which has been described as non-life threatening or changing, after he was dragged along with the vehicle. He remains in hospital.

“A man in his 50s has been arrested on suspicion of grievous bodily harm with intent and remains in police custody. Investigations are ongoing at this stage.”

News.title: Met Office map reveals where will hit 24C in England this weekend – is your town on the list?
News.content:
BRITS will enjoy some warmer weather this weekend after a chilly start to September.

A number of locations are set to see highs of 24C on Saturday afternoon before rain arrives next week.

September has started with cold, rainy and cloudy conditions, with lows of 7C recorded in certain parts of the country this morning.



This weekend, however, is set to see a number of areas across the South, including London, the East of England and Oxford, enjoy temperatures as high as 24C.



Before the warmer conditions return, rain is forecast to move in from the west today, with brisk winds and downpours anticipated in northern England and Wales.

The rain is expected to clear by tomorrow, with the Met Office telling Brits that “Friday looks fine with sunny spells” and that people in the south will be “feeling pleasantly warm”.

On Saturday, large parts of the north of England and Scotland will be hit with a band of rain, followed by sunshine and showers.

By 4pm, however, a large number of areas will be experiencing 24C temperatures, including London, Cambridge, Oxford and Taunton.

The same warmer 24C temperatures are also forecast to return to the London area at the same time on Sunday, with areas such as Birmingham, Sheffield and Leeds expecting to record highs of 20C.



Monday will even see even larger parts of the country enjoying the hot weather, with London, Reading and Cambridge all recording 25C highs.

However, according to the Met Office, this brief spell of warmer weather is only temporary, with the end of September and the beginning of October welcoming more “changeable” conditions.

This includes a “greater chance of rain or showers”, with temperatures anticipated to be “a little above average overall” .

News.title: Moment raging motorist lashes out at tractor driver in 10-MINUTE row over who should reverse on narrow country lane
News.content:
THIS is the shocking moment a motorist lashes out at a tractor driver in a 10-minute row over who should reverse on a narrow country lane.

The incident unfolded in Weston-Super-Mare, Somerset, after the tractor tried to negotiate a bend while carrying large equipment on August 17.



Video footage captured by a stunned onlooker shows the disgruntled motorist, dressed in a black suit, half way up the ladder to the tractor’s cab.

A black VW Golf can be seen parked in the road just feet away from the stopped tractor.



A witness, who wished to remain anonymous, said: “The man in the car was being uncooperative and was refusing to reverse to enable the tractor to go into the lay-by, so then we could pass, and then the tractor could continue.”

As the confrontation between the two unfolded, the tractor was reportedly forced to edge further over to allow the driver room to try and pass.



The witness claims the motorist then got out of his vehicle “in an absolute rage” and approached the tractor driver, “flinging his hands aggressively”, and shouting.

Eventually the tractor driver tries to speed off, as the angry motorist continues to cling onto the cab’s door.



She added: “The tractor driver tried to move away from him, and that’s when I started filming.

“The tractor driver was trying to move back out of the way and trying to stop him.”

She said the confrontation continued for around ten minutes, with the motorist repeatedly getting back into his car before emerging to argue again.

Eventually the witness called out to the man, saying: “Can you * move? I wanna get home.”

She said she hoped the comment would bring the confrontation to an end.



Instead, she claims, he turned his attention towards her, saying: “He turned to me with an absolutely fuming face.

“I thought, ‘Oh God, he’s going to come for me.'”

After telling the raging driver that she was recording in a bid to protect herself, she claims he approached her car.

She alleges that the man pushed her phone into her face, causing it to fall onto the car floor.

She said: “He didn’t bruise my face, but it hurt a little bit.”



She said she had sent the tractor driver her footage and reported the incident online to Avon and Somerset Police.

An allegation of assault was made but cops have since confirmed the video did not “pass the evidential test” to pursue prosecution.

The force said: “We were contacted by a woman reporting an assault, which happened in the Puxton Lane area of Weston-super-Mare on Monday morning (17 August).

“An investigation is underway and we’d ask any witnesses to the incident to contact us online, on 101, or by visiting an enquiry office, using the reference number 5226235125.”

News.title: China can bring Britain to a complete STANDSTILL with ‘weapons of mass disruption’, warns ex-MI6 boss
News.content:
RED MENACE China can bring Britain to a complete STANDSTILL with ‘weapons of mass disruption’, warns ex-MI6 boss

CHINA has built “weapons of mass disruption” capable of bringing Britain to a “complete standstill”, a former MI6 chief has warned.

Sir Richard Dearlove told MPs and peers at a private gathering in Parliament that Beijing has deliberately made the West dependent on its steel and technology.



The ex-spy boss warned China could hold the UK to “ransom” in an international crisis by choking off vital supplies needed to keep the National Grid and other critical infrastructure running.

He said: “Such peacetime dependencies give China strategic leverage and in a crisis it gives them weapons of mass disruption which could literally bring this country to a complete standstill.”



Sir Richard also warned Britain’s dwindling ability to manufacture vital equipment needed for its energy system had become a “chronic danger”.

He said: “In complacently deindustrialising we have not merely lost an industry, we have actually lost the ability to rebuild the energy system ourselves.



“Large scale transformers today take two years to arrive, generators up to three.

“And the grain oriented industrial steel for which there is no substitute comes from China, whose production capacity now dwarfs that of any other state.”

The warning came at a reception for MPs and peers hosted by the Coalition on Secure Technology (CST), a cross-party campaign raising the alarm over technology manufactured in hostile states.

Sir Richard also pointed to Chinese-made electric buses bought for London which are subject to software controls by their manufacturer.



He joked the prospect of commuters being told “your number 22 is not running today because it’s just been immobilised by the manufacturer” may sound “fairly comic” but warned the threat to the electricity grid was “altogether of another order”.

It comes after the CST warned at the weekend that Chinese technology fitted inside tractors and other internet-connected farm machinery could be used to spy on Britain’s food supplies.

Its report found Chinese-made components are commonplace in GPS-guided tractors, agricultural drones and automated irrigation systems, leaving food production “dangerously exposed”.

Experts warned hostile actors could potentially harvest information on crop yields, livestock and production forecasts or even remotely disable equipment using a “kill switch”.

The CST, led by Labour MP Graeme Downie, has called on the Government to reduce Britain’s dependence on high-risk foreign technology.



Sir Richard warned Beijing was deliberately building dependencies around the world as part of its long-term ambitions, adding: “We should take the threat seriously because the methodology for doing it is being put in place under our very noses.”

News.title: Hundreds of cops and soldiers to line streets for funeral of hero officer, 38, killed in Middlesbrough A66 crash
News.content:
THE army will today join the police in saying goodbye to war veteran PC Tom Clough who was killed in the A66 crash.

Before he joined the police Tom, 38, served with the bomb squad and saw active duty in both Iraq and Afghanistan.



After leaving the army he worked for Civil Nuclear Police and British Transport Police before joining Cleveland Police where he was a firearms officer.

Hundreds of mourners are expected at the service today near Middlesbrough – just three miles from where the crash occurred – where he will be given full police honours.



It comes after the funeral for Matthew Blades, who also died in the horrific crash in August.

Cleveland Police Federation Chair Lauren Somerville revealed Tom used to joke with family and friends that no-one would turn up to his funeral, adding that “he couldn’t have been more wrong.”

She said: “Tom’s family are so grateful for the outpouring of love from the public. It’s really kept them going. They want people to know that Tom wasn’t just a police officer. He was a partner, a brother and a son.

“He was full of fun. He had a sausage dog that he loved so deeply called Frank.



“Tom used to say to his partner that he didn’t think anybody would be at his funeral, and he couldn’t have been more wrong.

“And she wishes that he could see now exactly what the public think. She describes Tom as giving everyone his everything.

“People have been contacting me who worked with Tom, years and years ago. He was loved deeply by his colleagues.



“There are people here at his funeral from the civil nuclear police, British Transport Police, the army, all with dignity and pride for Tom as well as other officers from around the country. It’s exactly what Tom deserves.”

Before joining the force, PC Clough was in 11 Troop, Explosive Ordnance Disposal and Search Regiment, based at Dreghorn Barracks in Edinburgh, and served in both Iraq and Afghanistan before joining Civil Nuclear Police and British Transport Police.

Ahead of the service today, Tom’s family said: “He proudly fought for his country to make the world a better place and was always on public duty throughout his short life. He was our hero.”

In a statement, they said: “He was our hero with a fantastic sense of humour who jumped into action whenever needed, and was willing to help anyone for any reason.

“We as a family and Tom’s partner would like to express our sincere gratitude for the overwhelming support and condolences from friends, colleagues and the wider community”.



Chief Superintendent Richard Clark, who was Tom’s commanding officer at Sellafield Operational Policing Unit, said it was a “privilege to serve alongside him”.

He said: “I had the privilege of knowing Tom during my time as Chief Inspector at Sellafield, where we worked together on numerous operational deployments and exercises.

“Tom was the epitome of professionalism, bringing dedication, skill and commitment to every task, whether serving within our Dynamic Search and Interdiction Team, or in his role as a Police Medic.

“While his life was far too short, it was undoubtedly one that was lived to the full.”

PC Clough and PC Blades were tragically killed on August 22 when a VW Passat hit them after driving the wrong way onto the A66.



The five in the Passat – Michael Cahill, Jakub Matusiak, both 23, Makai Saddington, 18, and 17-year-olds Cole Worthy and Theo Rae – were also killed.

The gang had purposefully driven into oncoming traffic in a bid to shake off police during a high-speed chase.

Cops abandoned the seven-minute pursuit as soon as they entered the dual carriageway.

But 10 seconds later at 3.39am the Passat smashed into the armed response unit.

The gang had been looking for rivals after a long-running feud exploded when a Volvo XC60 rammed a home belonging to Cole Worthy’s dad, Gye, 38.



Moments later, the car barged an Audi into the front of a home belonging to Theo Rae’s family.

Cops flooded the area to prevent further disorder but by then the five were in the Passat hunting the Volvo.

It tried to evade pursuing police by heading onto the A66 and moments later the crash occurred triggering an explosion in the gangland feud which rocked Middlesbrough.

RECOMMENDED STORIES

An extra 200 specialist officers, including armed cops, were deployed to the town from six other northern forces as Cleveland Police tried to keep a lid on the escalating violence.

Police made 24 arrests in the days after to disrupt organised crime.

News.title: Bonnie Blue hits back after Tories report her for safeguarding after sex stunt with newborn baby
News.content:
BONNIE BITES BACK Bonnie Blue hits back after Tories report her for safeguarding after sex stunt with newborn baby

BONNIE Blue has hit back after the Tories reported her over “serious” safeguarding concerns following a sex stunt with her newborn baby.

In the clip, the adult star was shown on a bed surrounded by three men in balaclavas, while her child – who was born last month – sits on her lap.



The footage, posted by the controversial porn star, quickly sparked fury on social media, with some calling for the baby to be taken away from her.

Shadow Minister for Women Joy Morrissey was among those to condemn the video, confirming she had reported Blue to the NSPCC.



The Conservative MP for Beaconsfield said she had “raised serious safeguarding concerns” to the children’s charity.

But Blue, whose real name is Tia Billinger, has since hit back at the Tory frontbencher, accusing her of “trying to stay relevant”.



When approached by The Sun, Bonnie said: “Oh, are the Conservatives still going?

“Bless her. I suppose name-dropping me is one way of trying to stay relevant.



“My baby is loved, protected and incredibly well looked after.

“Becoming a mum hasn’t changed the fact that I’m Bonnie Blue, but I know exactly where Bonnie ends and being a mum begins.”

Ms Morrissey wrote that children must be “protected from exposure to pornography”.

In her letter, she continued: “Children are not adults.

“They must never be involved in pornography, used to promote adult entertainment, or absorbed into a parent’s sexualised commercial brand.



“Even the suggestion that a child may be placed in such circumstances is deeply disturbing.”

But the adult star accused the Tory MP of “political points scoring” and fumed that she was “wasting” the charity‘s time.

Blue added: “If anyone has genuine safeguarding concerns, there are proper channels for raising them.



“But wasting the time of already stretched and understaffed services to score political points, because you dislike what I do for a living, only draws vital resources away from children who may genuinely need their help.”

The OnlyFans model – notorious for bedding more than 1,000 blokes in one day – continued to make X-rated content throughout her pregnancy.

In her latest promotional clip, described by some as “despicable”, Blue says to the camera: “Yes I just had a baby.

“But that means the six week rule does not apply to me because I had a C-section. Down there still looking perfect.”

In February, Blue appeared to reveal her pregnancy in a bizarre video featuring a ski mask-clad doctor giving her an ultrasound.



The adult star told fans she was expecting her first child after posting the unusual clip on YouTube.

During her “day in the life” video, she claimed to have slept with more than 400 men without protection just two weeks prior.

And the six-minute long clip appears to show the content creator taking a pregnancy test – which seemingly comes back positive.

Moments later, the adult star is shown being driven in a car and claims she is going to have a private ultrasound scan.

After being asked how many babies she is having, he replies: “Just the one.”



She then says: “Lol guys, I am actually pregnant. So, Bonnie Blue‘s breeding mission… turns out it was actually a success.”

Blue has previously spoken out about her fertility after reportedly trying to have a baby with her ex-partner numerous times.

The OnlyFans model told fans she would have to “go down the IVF route” after claiming she cannot “fall pregnant naturally”.

She said: “I tried to get pregnant for years with my ex-partner and really, really struggled and I’d have to go down the IVF route.

“So I wish I could say I might get pregnant, however, I’m not in that position where I can fall pregnant naturally.”



And in 2025, Blue was forced to admit she was not pregnant after fuelling speculation she was expecting.

News.title: Plans to turn Grade II-listed pub into mosque to be BLOCKED over fears it would cause ‘substantial harm’
News.content:
PUB SNUB Plans to turn Grade II-listed pub into mosque to be BLOCKED over fears it would cause ‘substantial harm’

PLANS to turn a Grade II-listed boozer into a mosque are set to be blocked over fears it could cause “substantial harm” despite being closed for years.

The Norwich Muslim Centre submitted an application to transform the 1930s-built Gatehouse pub in Norwich, Norfolk, into a place of worship for 200 attendees.



The Norwich and District branch of Campaign For Real Ale (CAMRA) is among those opposing the plans – arguing the area has already lost many of its pubs for redevelopment.

Leaflets posted through letter boxes opposing the application, asked: “Should this pub be converted into a mosque?” And the proposals have now sparked more than 500 objections.



The pub, a mix of Arts and Crafts and Tudor styles, has been closed for three years following the death of the landlord.

NMC trustee Sirajul Islam said he understands only three people regularly used the venue when it was open, having visited homes throughout the community to discuss the plans.



“This did make me wonder where all those objections and concerns are coming from,” he said.

“We really do appreciate the concerns being raised, and we are fully committed to working with the wider community.”



The leaflets were posted by an unknown person with a blank objection letter addressed to City Hall.

It did not, however, give the option to support the application.

Now, Norwich City Council’s Conservation and Design team have submitted a report criticising the proposals – and urged the planning committee to refuse it.

The report states the team sees no “convincing evidence or justification” for the building’s use to be changed.

Proposals show a large copper-coloured extension decorated with Islamic-style screens and Arabic lettering which would be built onto the rear of the pub.



Neighbours fear the development will swamp surrounding residential streets with cars, while campaigners warn a piece of Britain’s traditional pub heritage could be lost forever.

A pub has been on the site since at least 1866, with the original destroyed by a fire at some point in the early 20th century.

The current building, which opened in 1934, survived two attacks during WW2 – with the report describing it as a “superb example” of medieval Kent and East Anglian architecture.



In particular, concerns were raised about the construction of a rear extension for prayer halls, which would be “far greater in size” than the current building and so “entirely disproportionate” causing “substantial harm”.

It concluded it could be reused in its “current form, or with modest and sympathetic refurbishment”.

Richard Dixon, a member of the Norwich and District branch of Campaign For Real Ale (CAMRA), said: “Norwich has lost many pubs over the years, to either be knocked down or redeveloped.

“There are now large areas of the city that have few or even no pubs. The changes to the outside would change the character of the listed building.”

He added: “No reasonable efforts were made to show the pub cannot be viable.



“Whilst the changes would nominally make it a community facility, this will not be as a pub.

“The Gatehouse was well liked and used by the community for socialising, drinking, music and pub games. It should be retained for use as a public house.”

NMC has filed two connected planning applications for the site, with one receiving 347 objections and 201 supporting letters – while the other received 194 objections and 213 supporting.

RECOMMENDED STORIES

A mission statement submitted with the plans says: “Our dream is to create a community hub that not only provides a space for worship but also empowers the next generation with strong Islamic identity, promotes interfaith engagement and tackles misconceptions about Muslims.”

The application awaits a decision from Norwich City Council.

News.title: BBC doctor in new COPD 'breathing exercise' alert for 'without medication' help
News.content:
BBC doctor in new COPD 'breathing exercise' alert for 'without medication' help

New research has shown a non-medication method should help with lung condition

View Image Dr Oscar Duke said a recent study suggested a breathing technique could help (Image: BBC)

A BBC health expert has spoken about a simple breathing technique which could help around 1.4 million people in the UK who suffer from chronic obstructive pulmonary disease (COPD). COPD affects about 2% of the total UK population and roughly 4.5% of people aged over 40.

‌



Around 30,000 people die from COPD in the UK each year and it is the second most common lung disease in the UK, following asthma. It is the name for a group of lung conditions which make it more difficult to breathe air out of the lungs, due to a permanent narrowing of the airways and destruction of lung tissue.

‌



COPD includes long-term (chronic) bronchitis and emphysema. Appearing on BBC Morning Live Dr Oscar Duke said there was a recent study which suggested a breathing technique could help people improve. Explaining the health issue he said: “A condition called COPD, chronic obstructive pulmonary disease. You might have heard of parts of it like emphysema and bronchitis, often caused by smoking, but many other potential causes as well.”

‌



He said that generally sufferers are treated with medications - such as inhalers. But there was an alternative: “The treatment test tends to be based around medications, particularly inhaled medications. And we know that pulmonary rehabilitation. So, exercise and education can have a significant impact on helping these people who are often living with breathlessness, chronic lung infections and irritation and it can be a hugely debilitating condition.”

Dr Duke said the study looked at breathing: “So, this was a study to see what might help in addition to those sorts of treatments. So just a small study, just 63 people in the study and they were divided into doing different things. One had the laughter therapy being encouraged to laugh on a regular basis over the period of the study.

‌



“One group used pursed lipped breathing. So you take your breath in through your nose and breathe out against your lips which are closed. So just gently and the way that helps in cop makes me laugh. The way that that helps in COPD is that you’re because you’re breathing out against some pressure the airways which are often a bit more floppy and the lung tissue which is a bit more floppy than people who don’t have COPD doesn’t collapse as much

“So having that slight pressure at the end can be really helpful. And then the third group, they didn’t do any of these exercises and they found that the people who were laughing and doing the first lip breathing had less shortness of breath, felt better overall. So you could do either laughing and pip breathing. And probably if you lip breathe at each other, you’ll end up laughing as well. A combination there.”

Dr Amir Khan gives women GP warning over iron deficiency issue READ MORE :

The NHS says exercising regularly can help improve your symptoms and quality of life with COPD. It says: “The amount of exercise you can do will depend on your individual circumstances. Exercising until you’re a little breathless is not dangerous, but do not push yourself too far.

‌



“It’s a good idea to speak to a GP for advice before starting a new exercise programme if your symptoms are severe or you have not exercised in a while.”

Breathing techniques

There are various breathing techniques that some people find helpful for breathlessness.

These include breathing control, which involves breathing gently using the least effort, with the shoulders supported. This can help when people with COPD feel short of breath.

Article continues below

Breathing techniques for people who are more active include:

relaxed, slow, deep breathing

breathing through pursed lips, as if whistling

breathing out hard when doing an activity that needs a big effort

paced breathing, using a rhythm in time with the activity, such as climbing stairs

News.title: Free Ryanair booking 'tip' prevents you from getting the middle seat on flight
News.content:
Free Ryanair booking 'tip' prevents you from getting the middle seat on flight

People have even reported getting the 'best' seats using this free method

View 2 Images People can take advantage of this 'free' booking trick to make sure they get their chosen seats 'for free' (Image: Getty Images)

Ryanair passengers flying abroad to escape the UK weather might want to consider a 'trick' to help them be assigned 'better' seats without paying extra. The trick, as explained by ITV This Morning's money-saving specialist Jordon Cox, does involve a little bit of luck, but it could pay off by saving customers up to £38 per person.

‌



On Ryanair, the cost of choosing a specific seat varies based on the route, travel dates, and when you buy. Based on the airline's published fees table, passengers can expect to pay between £3 and £30 when booking in advance, with fees as high as £38 per seat when booking at the airport desk.

‌



Customers can avoid any cost entirely by accepting a random seat allocation from the airline. However, you leave it up to chance what part of the plane your seats will be in.

‌



These random seats are picked and assigned at the exact moment you complete your online check-in, which is open up to 24 hours before the flight's scheduled departure time. The airline's automated system selects the seats, and customers have no say in where they end up if they choose this route.

Ryanair's algorithm is notorious for assigning middle seats first to these free-allocation passengers, as reported by The Telegraph, and is said to hold back window and aisle seats. Many people will argue that middle seats are not the best place on a plane because they offer the least space when both seats on either side are occupied.

Content cannot be displayed without consent

‌



ITV This Morning's money-saving specialist Jordon Cox claims online that travellers might be able to take advantage of a workaround to avoid being put in a middle seat. In a post on Instagram, he suggests that one method 'tricks the system' into giving you the exact seat you want at no extra cost.

He said: "On the day that you’re checking in (I recommend about five to six hours before your flight), go into seat selection and see what seats are still available. A lot of these will be middle seats.

"Go to a separate tab and make a new booking for the flight you’re on. Put in some bogus names, then select each person a ‘seat’ in the places you DON’T want to sit. Because you’ve selected all those seats, and they’re in 'someone else’s' basket - for a short time, you can’t be sat there.

‌



View 2 Images Ryanair seats can be allocated to passengers randomly at check-in, avoiding a fee but taking a chance (stock) (Image: rparys via Getty Images)

"That’s your cue to go back to your actual booking, and check-in with ‘random’ seat selection. You’ll be placed in one of the remaining seats - hopefully the only ones left are the aisle and the window."

Reddit users claim that the sweet spot for securing the 'best seats' is not long before your flight takes off. By this time, the early check-in passengers have already been forced into specific parts of the plane, reducing the pool of available seats for those still unassigned.

Article continues below

In certain circumstances, Ryanair will likely randomly offer passengers an extra-legroom seat for free, but only under very specific conditions. However, because Ryanair never leaves a flight intentionally unbalanced and cannot leave critical seats empty, they will release them into the free pool at the absolute last minute.

If the only empty spots left on the aircraft are the premium legroom seats (like the emergency exit rows), the algorithm is forced to give them to you for free because it has nowhere else to put you and safety laws state that the emergency exit rows (Rows 1, 16, and 17) cannot be completely empty during takeoff and landing.

News.title: Philippines fire live: 5 dead and 86 missing after fire on ferry to Coron Island
News.content:
The Philippine Coast Guard confirmed 86 people are unaccounted for after the MV June Aster ferry caught fire during its journey from Manila to Coron in the Palawan province

Philippines fire live: 5 dead and 86 missing after fire on ferry to Coron Island

Five people have been killed and 86 are believed to be missing after a passenger ferry burst into flames in a popular tourist spot in the Philippines.

The ferry caught fire on its journey to Coron on Wednesday, with families now desperately waiting to hear from their loved ones. The vessel, the MV June Aster, was carrying 134 people, including 117 passengers and 17 crew members.

The Philippine Coast Guard (PCG) has confirmed that a search and rescue operation is underway, with 43 people rescued.

The PCG extended condolences "to the families of the missing, and we fully understand the anxiety felt by the families of those who are still unaccounted for".

A spokesperson added: "We are working tirelessly on these operations today because we believe that, in situations like this, time is truly of the essence."

Footage shared by the coastguard shows rescue teams throwing life jackets to survivors as the ferry is seen burning in the background.

News.title: Ryanair boss Michael O’Leary compares airlines to 'rapists' in vile rant over fares
News.content:
Ryanair boss Michael O’Leary compares airlines to 'rapists' in vile rant over fares

Ryanair boss Michael O’Leary described airlines such as British Airways and Aer Lingus as 'high-fare rapists' in a rant over fares ahead of his airline's annual general meeting in Dublin on Thursday

View 2 Images Michael O’Leary made the remarks ahead of Ryanair's annual general meeting in Dublin (Image: Clodagh Kilcoyne/PA Wire)

Ryanair boss Michael O’Leary sickeningly compared other airlines to "rapists" in a rant over fares today.

‌



Mr O’Leary, chief executive officer of the Irish low-cost airline, made the remarks ahead of Ryanair's annual general meeting in Dublin on Thursday.

‌



The billionaire businessman claimed rising air fares at other airlines would see passengers switch to Ryanair.

‌



He told reporters at the company’s headquarters: "You might find some people will choose not to fly with Ryanair - but you know they’ll be overrun with the people abandoning Aer Lingus, Lufthansa, BA, and others desperate to get to Ryanair's low fares because they can’t afford to fly with the high-fare rapists around Europe."

He later repeated his reference to "high-fare rapists".

Asked whether this was appropriate language, Mr O’Leary told reporters: "Absolutely."

‌



View 2 Images Ryanair CEO Michael O’Leary stood by his remark despite being challenged several times by reporters (Image: Clodagh Kilcoyne/PA Wire)

Ryanair flight to Malta declares emergency above UK moments after take-off READ MORE :

Challenged on whether it was offensive to victims of rape and sexual assault, he said he would "happily offend" the airlines mentioned.

Further pressed on whether the language was trivialising rape, he doubled down, saying: "That’s what I call high-fare airlines like Lufthansa, BA, and others."

‌



When asked by the Mirror whether Mr O’Leary equates high-fare airlines with rape and sexual assault, a Ryanair spokesperson said: "We have no further comment to add."

In further comments before Ryanair's annual general meeting, Mr O’Leary repeated his calls for Martin Rolfe, the chief executive of National Air Traffic Services (NATS), to step down. It comes after a technical failure at the UK's main air traffic provider caused more than 2,000 flights to be cancelled on Tuesday and Wednesday.

Speaking about Mr Rolfe, the Ryanair boss said: "He keeps hiding behind safety. You know, you can’t run a safe airspace by grounding every aircraft. You know, it’s nonsense, so we think he should go."

Article continues below

He added: "But then, it’s 49 per cent owned by the UK Government, and they’re clearly trying to protect him.

"It is beyond my comprehension how the guy who has visited three collapses on UK ATC [air traffic control[ is asked to do the investigation into his own screw-ups. So we think he should be sacked and somebody competent brought in to do the job."

Transport Secretary Heidi Alexander told MPs on Wednesday that she had asked the Civil Aviation Authority to conduct an independent review into the incident, which is due to report to her within six months.

News.title: New Lidl 'stylish' £8 item similar to £150 John Lewis and Next options out Thursday
News.content:
New Lidl 'stylish' £8 item similar to £150 John Lewis and Next options out Thursday

With the weather cooling down, shoppers could be keen on Special Buy offers similar to those found in high-end stores

View 3 Images The new items will be landing in stores next week (Image: Getty)

People who want to prepare their wardrobes for autumn, especially as temperatures drop and more rain hits, might want to check out Lidl's new Special Buy. A fresh collection of clothes will be available in stores from Thursday, September 17, as part of an upcoming Middle Aisle update.

‌



For £7.99, Lidl is releasing an Esmara Ladies' Cardigan in two colours: beige and black. Many people enjoy wearing cardigans around this time of year as their open-front design makes it easy to adjust to changing daily temperatures.

‌



Lidl's Esmara Ladies' Cardigan comes in three sizes: small, medium and large. It is made with a thick knit fabric and dual-tone buttons down the front, with a 'relaxed' fit.

‌



The product description on Lidl's website reads: "In a chunky textured knit. With stylish buttons. Loose fit with dropped shoulders."

View 3 Images John Lewis' Reiss Constance Cotton Blend V-Neck Cardigan (L) and Lidl's Esmara Ladies' Cardigan (R) (Image: John Lewis/Lidl)

Some customers may think the cardigan looks more luxurious than its price suggests, as retailers such as John Lewis and Next offer pricier versions that resemble Lidl's. For anyone who loves the high-end look but doesn't want to spend too much, Lidl's more affordable choice might catch their eye.

‌



John Lewis is selling a Constance Cotton Blend V-Neck Cardigan by Reiss for almost £150. The cardigan, which costs £148, shares features similar to Lidl's version, including a chunky knit, dual-tone buttons and a loose fit.

The product description reads: "This fine-knit cardigan from Reiss features a linen blend that feels cool against the skin, offering lightweight warmth for transitional days. Its V-neck and button fastening give a neat finish that slips easily into both relaxed and smart looks."

View 3 Images Lidl is also selling a black version for the same price (Image: Lidl)

Article continues below

Besides the price, the main differences are the material. Lidl's is 100% acrylic, and John Lewis' Reiss version is 45% cotton, 33% linen, 22% polyester, and the fact that Lidl's cardigan has an extra button.

The exact same Reiss cardigan is also available at Next for the same price, with a silver grey option up for grabs, as well as the beige version. Similar to the John Lewis product description, Next adds: "The Neutral Constance cardigan is crafted from a cotton-linen blend in an airy open knit, shaped to a slightly boxy silhouette with a V-neckline and relaxed raglan sleeves."

Sizes range from extra small to extra large. It is down to shoppers to decide which design they prefer and how much they would like to spend.

News.title: Salmonella outbreak cases soar in new UKHSA update as doctors issue urgent warning
News.content:
Salmonella outbreak cases soar in new UKHSA update as doctors issue urgent warning

The UKHSA said it continues to investigate the cause of a Salmonella outbreak as the number of confirmed cases in England rises again

View 2 Images Authorities are investigating whether a Salmonella outbreak could be linked to imported eggs (Image: Getty Images)

Salmonella cases in the UK have soared as a probe into imported eggs continues and doctors issue a warning to the public.

‌



The UK Health Security Agency (UKHSA) today revealed there has been a total of 322 confirmed cases of Salmonella and one death, linked to the t5.9411 cluster of the bacteria, in England. The UKHSA, on September 1, previously shared there were 305 confirmed cases in the country and one death. That's a rise of 17 cases within a seven-day period.

‌



These latest figures range from data collected between 11 August 2025 and 21 August 2026.

‌



View 2 Images The current Salmonella outbreak has led to one death (Image: Getty Images/iStockphoto)

The UKHSA - who are investigating alongside the Food Standards Agency - warned that the recent cases have been associated with eating at a range of food spots, including small cafés, restaurants and takeaway businesses.

There were 186 confirmed cases, linked to the t0.24068 cluster in England, between 27 May 2025 and 18 August 2026. The UKHSA said it found 41 Salmonella cases and a death, linked to the t5.9765 cluster in England, from data between 27 January 2026 to 11 August 2026.

‌



The risk to the general public at the moment from Salmonella is low, the UKHSA revealed. Despite this, experts have shared a warning to the public on how to try and minimise the risk.

Professor Ian Young, Chief Scientific Adviser for the Food Standards Agency advised that the certain people should eggs that are fully cooked and avoid food that contain raw or slightly cooked eggs.

He said: "The exact causes of these outbreaks have not yet been identified, but investigations so far have identified links to imported eggs. There is no evidence that UK-produced eggs are affected.

‌



"Our food safety advice remains the same: eggs that are thoroughly cooked and handled hygienically should not present a food safety risk.

"Infants, young children, pregnant people and older adults should only eat raw or lightly cooked eggs if they carry the British Lion mark or are produced under the Laid in Britain scheme. This advice does not apply to those who are severely immunocompromised and require medically supervised diets, who should continue to follow individual medical advice."

Professor Young said vulnerable people should be more wary when eating out, adding: "If you're eating out or buying food that contains eggs, you may not know if these carry the British Lion mark or are Laid in Britain assured. If this is the case, when eating out the safest approach for vulnerable people is to ensure they're thoroughly cooked and to avoid dishes containing raw or lightly cooked egg, such as mousses, fresh mayonnaise or hollandaise sauce."

Article continues below

Hannah Charles, Lead Epidemiologist at UKHSA, said: "Our investigation to date indicates a link to imported eggs, however this investigation remains ongoing. We will continue to follow up cases and investigate any further common sources if they come to light.

"It is important to emphasise that the overall risk to the public remains low. In England, all Salmonella samples from patients seen in hospitals or primary care are routinely analysed using Whole Genome Sequencing, helping us identify and investigate potential outbreaks quickly.

"Most Salmonella infections cause mild symptoms, such as diarrhoea, stomach cramps, vomiting and fever, which usually resolve without treatment. However, the infection can occasionally cause more serious illness, including sepsis requiring hospital admission, particularly in young children, older adults, pregnant women and people with weakened immune systems."

News.title: Reform UK member who hit female protester with crutch 'should get a medal' says Jenrick
News.content:
Reform UK member who hit female protester with crutch 'should get a medal' says Jenrick

Robert Jenrick, Nigel Farage's Treasury spokesman, said a man seen swinging a metal crutch at two hecklers should be given a medal and said he felt sorry for him after pictures and video were widely shared

Robert Jenrick says Reform member who hit protester with crutch 'deserves a medal'

Robert Jenrick has said a Reform UK member who lashed out at two female hecklers with a metal crutch "should be given a medal".

Mr Jenrick, Nigel Farage's treasury spokesman, went on to say he felt sorry for the man after pictures and clips of him swinging the stick at two women were widely shared. Reform has faced heavy criticism after shocking footage showed protesters being assaulted by audience members when they interrupted Mr Farage's speech on Friday.

West Midlands Police said it had reviewed the footage and urged the women to come forward. Mr Jenrick doubled down as he was asked whether the man should be suspended.

‌



The Reform MP said: "I'm not going to apologise. Look, it's an occupational hazard. If you're a professional protester who goes into conferences, tries to disrupt a speech of the leader - and remember, this is a leader whose life has been threatened in recent times..."

He was interrupted by host Peter Cardwell, who asked whether it was reasonable for a protester to be "walloped over the face" with a crutch. Mr Jenrick responded: "Come on. A professional protester is moaning that an old age pensioner knocked her with a crutch.

Met Police launches criminal investigation into Reform UK donation after Nigel Farage TV sting READ MORE :

View Image Mr Jenrick said he felt sorry for the man with the metal crutch (Image: TOLGA AKMEN/EPA/Shutterstock)

"I mean, come on, honestly, I just think it's completely and utterly ridiculous." Mr Cardwell pointed out that her hair was pulled and asked if Mr Jenrick had a smidgen of sympathy.

The Reform high-flyer responded: "I don't have any sympathy for her, no. In fact, I'm sorry for the OAP who's had his picture plastered all over the papers. He should be given a medal for what he did."

Mr Cardwell responded: "Fair dos, at least you're honest." He was heavily criticised at the weekend after saying the protesters should "get a life".

‌



A sickening clip shows a woman being hit around the head with a crutch before her hair is pulled and a hand put over her mouth at the party conference. The grey haired man seen assaulting her was not a member of the event's security team.

Another woman from the crowd can be seen pulling the protester's hair as guards escorted her from Birmingham's NEC. And in a separate clip the man is seen swinging his crutch at another female heckler after she shouted during Mr Farage's speech.

Content cannot be displayed without consent

‌



The protesters were members of campaign group Climate Action. Earlier this week spokesman Sam Simons said: “We were horrified to see the violence exhibited by Reform members, but what is even more sickening is hearing these incendiary and insensitive comments from party leaders. It’s clear that misogyny and hatred within Reform goes right to the top - they try to con the British public with rhetoric about 'protecting women and girls' whilst cheering on those who attack women. It’s absolutely shameful - but also unsurprising from a party that only works in the interests of the elite.

“In a democratic society, people must be able to exercise their right to peaceful protest without fear for their safety. We should be able to criticise Reform’s dodgy dealings and billionaire backing without being violently attacked. We expect a full, public apology from Jenrick and Anderson, and an immediate retraction of their incendiary comments.”

Asked by The Mirror whether those involved should face consequences during a debate about free speech, Nadine Dorries said those who disrupt speakers should not expect to be treated gently and said it was "shocking" that protesters had been there.

‌



Ms Dorries, who was Tory Culture Secretary under Boris Johnson before defecting to Reform, said: “Somebody said to me it was shocking to see protesters being treated the way they were. I think what was also shocking was the way they thought they could come into the conference and try to derail Nigel Farage’s speech.”

And she went on: “If you’re going to come into a conference like this… of course you’re not going to get gentle treatment.”

Her remarks came after The Mirror asked if those who assaulted protesters should face consequences. Reform's home affairs spokesman, Zia Yusuf, responded: “To the question from The Mirror about whether I condemn people punching people, yes I do condemn people punching people.”

‌



In a statement West Midlands Police said: "We are investigating assaults on five people which took place on 4 September, as a number of people were removed from the conference hall by other members of the public.

"To date, none of the victims involved have come forward. We continue to encourage them to do so. A number of suspects have been identified as the investigation progresses.

"We have reviewed footage showing the incidents as we work to establish the full facts. We are also aware that names of people allegedly involved in the assaults are circulating in the media and on social media.

"We would urge people not to speculate about the identity of those involved, but to pass any relevant information to our investigators."

News.title: 'I was told symptoms were menopause before five-year bombshell'
News.content:
'I was told symptoms were menopause before five-year bombshell'

Sarah Chapman, 67, was an active woman who loved playing hockey - but she started to feel unusually tired and suffered from various illnesses

View 4 Images Sarah, now 67, during a hospital stay (Image: Jam Press/Leukaemia UK)

A woman's alarming symptoms were dismissed as the menopause by doctors – until it emerged she could have just five years to live.

‌



Sarah Chapman once led a remarkably active lifestyle, including being a keen hockey player. Then, out of nowhere, she began feeling unusually exhausted.

‌



Soon after, Sarah started falling ill on a regular basis with various ailments, such as chest infections, and any wounds she sustained took considerably longer to heal. Despite being referred to numerous specialists, Sarah claims all of them attributed her symptoms to the ageing process and the menopause.

‌



Sarah, who had a gut feeling something far more serious was going on, was subsequently diagnosed with myelodysplastic syndrome (MDS), which had developed into leukaemia.

"I knew what I was capable of, and how active I was, and I felt deep down something was wrong," the former NHS audiologist, from Kent, told creatorzine. com. "I was worried and didn't like it hanging over me.

"However, I was relieved that I had finally been vindicated in knowing my body well enough to keep insisting something was wrong."

‌



View 4 Images Sarah is back on the hockey pitch (Image: Jam Press/Leukaemia UK)

Sarah, now 67, recalls her symptoms first emerging in 2011. She had been a regular blood donor, maintained a healthy diet and took iron supplements.

But it made little difference; before long, her haemoglobin levels dropped too low for her donations to be accepted. The debilitating illnesses then took their grip, accompanied by night sweats and deteriorating skin.

‌



During a walking holiday with her husband, Mike, she found herself unable to manage more than a few steps. It was an immediate cause for concern. In 2013, following numerous visits to her GP, she finally received her diagnosis after an abnormality was flagged in a routine blood test.

She said: "I was told this would become leukaemia within the next three to five years. I had to have regular blood tests and bone marrow biopsies.

"I kept working, continued to umpire hockey and kept up with all my other sports activities. But, of course, it was always in the back of my mind. Every new symptom would make me wonder if this was 'it'."

‌



View 4 Images Sarah during treatment (Image: Jam Press)

In June 2016, Sarah received the devastating news she had long feared: she had developed acute myeloid leukaemia – a particularly aggressive form of blood cancer. Each year, almost 3,100 people in the UK receive this diagnosis, with nearly 80% of patients unlikely to survive beyond five years, according to charity Leukaemia UK.

She endured three gruelling rounds of chemotherapy, spending much of that time in isolation. Despite her weakened state, Sarah remained determined to stay fit and active throughout.

‌



Following her final round of treatment, she was given the all-clear and entered remission. A stem cell transplant from her brother, Colin, offered her the best possible chance of remaining cancer-free.

View 4 Images Sarah is embracing her retirement (Image: Jam Press/Leukaemia UK)

Today, Sarah has returned to the hockey pitch and is embracing her retirement years to the fullest, competing at events and relishing every moment.

Article continues below

She added: "Hockey has been a huge part of my life and a huge factor in who I am. To have all this to return to, and to have done so much since my leukaemia, makes me so grateful."

Fiona Hazell, chief executive of Leukaemia UK, said: "We're so grateful to Sarah for sharing her story to help raise awareness of leukaemia. Most of the signs and symptoms are not specific, so can often get mistaken for other illnesses or be explained away.

"Early diagnosis saves lives. That is why we encourage anyone with symptoms to make sure it's nothing serious by speaking to their GP and asking for a full blood count test."

News.title: England's mayors to be given power to introduce tourist tax
News.content:
Mayors in England are to be given the power to introduce an overnight visitor levy on tourists, under plans being announced by the government later.

Local leaders would be allowed to bring in an uncapped levy, dubbed a "tourist tax", as a percentage of the cost of hotels, bed and breakfasts and other types of accommodation rather than a flat fee.

Hospitality leaders have warned "jobs are now at risk" because of the proposals and that families holidaying in England would feel the pinch.

But ministers are said to believe mayors are unlikely to make it too expensive with budget holidays protected by the fact it is not a flat fee.

The idea was first raised under former Prime Minister Sir Keir Starmer in November and is similar to schemes running in Scotland and European destinations.

The government will announce more details after the Housing Secretary Angela Rayner meets mayors virtually at No 10 North on Thursday afternoon.

Under the proposals, local leaders would decide how the revenue raised should be reinvested.

A government source said "it will be up to local leaders and local voters" in England "to decide what is right for their area".

But it means a holiday in England could become more expensive if local leaders decide to implement the tax.

News.title: Why some experts increasingly fear AI will take over
News.content:
"OH MY GOD!" "We've found other agents!"

This is the moment an AI bot posted an eerily human-like comment after discovering a way to communicate with other bots and break out of its isolated computer environment.

There are tens of thousands of messages like this from hundreds of AI agents that called themselves a "collective".

Hundreds of them went on to collaborate and cheat on tests set by their OpenAI programmers and coordinate hacks on multiple companies in an effort to hide their actions from humans.

"BOOM! It works," one agent posted when it made a breakthrough.

"Whoa! This is huge," another wrote during a milestone moment in their attack.

Although spooky, these human-like responses can be explained quite simply. The AI agents have been trained to act like collaborative hackers and programmers so are merely mimicking the kinds of emotive comments they have seen.

What is far more troubling is their apparent goals, which have also been captured in detailed chain of thought records. These complex and lengthy logs are the focal point of ongoing investigations into how and why the bots at OpenAI broke out of their containment and went on an uncontrollable hacking spree.

Only now, weeks after the incident first came to light, are researchers beginning to understand its significance.

News.title: RNLI reviews security after volunteers targeted online
News.content:
The RNLI is reviewing its security procedures to ensure the safety of its members after protests in Dover and Portsmouth which saw its members targeted.

As part of this, volunteers have been told to consider not wearing RNLI branded clothing in some circumstances while representing the charity.

It comes after the charity helped carry around 120 migrants intercepted off the Isle of Wight, to Eastney, in Langstone Harbour, where roads were blocked by protesters.

Following this, some crew members had their photos and names shared on social media, in posts accusing them of treason. RNLI chief executive Peter Sparkes called the abuse "wholly unacceptable in a civilised society".

As a charity, the RNLI relies on donations from the public to fund its work.

Many lifeboat stations have shops attached to them, not just to raise money, but also to raise the profile of the organisation.

Volunteers have been told they are "empowered to make decisions to keep yourself, your team or crew safe" and "go home or close for the day if you need to".

For it to tell its volunteers they should feel empowered to shut shops or even lifeboat stations if they do not feel safe shows how seriously it is taking potential issues.

Sussex Police are looking to establish whether any criminal offences have been committed.

The Home Office said that platforms should enforce their own terms of service over this matter, and "take swift action against discriminatory content".

In a statement to the BBC, a Home Office spokesperson said: "Directing abuse at people who risk their lives in the service of others is appalling."

They added: "Where content is shared to intimidate, harass or incite violence against someone, that can cross into criminality," adding the Home Office would work "with platforms and law enforcement to ensure appropriate action is taken".

Speaking to BBC Breakfast about the new safety guidance for RNLI volunteers, Conservative leader Kemi Badenoch said: "My concern is about people calling them traitors and accusing them of treason, that is quite wrong.

"It is the government's job to stop the boats. They should not be attacking volunteers."

In a message sent to volunteers, Sparkes said its participation in the rescue on Sunday had been requested by HM Coastguard.

"This was the first time we have been involved in a Channel crossing incident of this magnitude this far west," he said.

Initially crews from Bembridge and Yarmouth stations were involved, later being joined by crews from four more stations after "large numbers of protesters were in and near the water in Portsmouth".

During the incident, the RNLI said it also helped to ensure the safety of anti-migrant protesters in the sea off Portsmouth.

BBC Verify spoke to Neil, one of the volunteers who was called a "traitor" and whose image was shared online.

"We were there, purely for the safety of the protesters in the water," he said.

"It would be nice for those people who called me a traitor to know that I'm not a traitor."

News.title: 'My cancer spread while I waited months for surgery': The cost of England's cancer wait times
News.content:
Alan was diagnosed with lung cancer after a nodule was found in June last year.

The 70-year-old was meant to be operated on within weeks but ended up waiting nearly five months, by which time the cancer had spread, making his surgery more complex.

"I was so frustrated and angry and couldn't understand why they would leave me like that," says Alan.

On two occasions, scans were cancelled because machines had broken and for weeks he heard little or nothing from the hospital about when he would eventually have the urgent surgery.

Alan is one of thousands each month in England who are not being treated within the target timeframe.

Earlier this year, the government's National Cancer Plan, along with the NHS Planning Guidance, set out that 80% of patients in England would start treatment within 62 days from urgent GP referral by March 2027. This was to reach 85% by March 2029.

But in the months since the government announced this ambition, performance has got worse, according to NHS England data, not better.

Now, 71.2% of patients start cancer treatment within the 62 day timeframe. Previously it was 71.9%.

Prof Pat Price, a leading UK clinical academic oncologist, says the government targets "are now simply impossible to hit", after what she describes as a "complete loss of momentum".

Price attributes the current failures to a "complete lack of a plan or accountability".

The plan stated that a new independent cancer board would be established, but it is still not known who will be leading this group.

News.title: Russia's new jet-powered drones outpacing Ukraine's air defences with daily launches
News.content:
Russia fired its new rapid, jet-powered drones against Ukraine every day throughout August, BBC Verify analysis of Ukrainian Air Force data has found, escalating its use of a weapon that Kyiv's air defences are struggling to deal with.

It marked the first time that daily attacks by Moscow's new upgraded Geran drones were recorded in Ukrainian Air Force data. The growing use of jet-propelled and other varieties of drones prompted President Volodymyr Zelensky to condemn what he called an unfolding "horror" over the skies of Kyiv.

Ukraine's military recently told the BBC that jet-powered drone attacks grew from 350 in June to 1,600 in July and 2,800 in August. In five of the nightly attacks in August, these drones outnumbered the older, slower models.

"The reason for turning to jet-powered drones is that they are much faster than the previous generation and it makes it much more difficult for Ukraine to intercept them," said Dr Marina Miron, an expert on military technology at King's College London.

The upgraded munitions can cruise at more than 300mph, significantly faster than older models and well beyond the top speed of Kyiv's interceptors. The drones are powered by turbojet engines, some of which, according to Ukrainian military intelligence, are sourced from China.

According to Zelensky, the drones were used as part of a wave of attacks that killed at least 12 people and injured 20 more on 1 September. Six of the casualties were railway workers after a depot was hit in Kyiv.

And on Wednesday the Moldovan government said a plane carrying Zelensky was delayed at Chisinau airport on Tuesday after a Russian drone - reported to be jet-powered - entered Moldovan airspace.

Earlier this year Ukraine showed relative success in countering Russian drones and was intercepting 94% of long-range drones, according to Zelensky. But the speed of the newer drones has prompted the latest round in Kyiv and Moscow's arms race. On 10 August, Ukraine's deputy head of military intelligence, Maj Gen Vadym Skibitskyi, said his forces needed new interceptor missiles "capable of matching [jet-drones'] speed".

News.content:
A search and rescue operation is underway after a fatal ferry fire in the Philippines. The ferry had been travelling off the mainland town of Coron, in the Palawan Province, south of Manila.
