News.title: Primark finally set to launch home deliveries
News.content:
Primark has said it plans to launch a home delivery service in Britain, four years after it made its first foray into e-commerce.

The retailer did not say when it expects to launch the service, but it has bought a warehouse in Sheffield from to enable it to ship products to homes.

The company said there was "opportunity for profitable growth" through home deliveries, which could help boost trade after Primark reported subdued sales following the recent hot weather.

Analysts said the decision to offer home delivery after years of resistance - including through the pandemic - indicated that Primark was facing major challenges from ultra-fast-fashion brands such as Shein.

Primark did not sell goods online until 2022, when it launched a click-and-collect service which meant shoppers still had to travel to pick up their purchases.

Associated British Foods (ABF), which owns Primark, said the fashion chain would "continue to grow click and collect and... will in the future offer home delivery in Great Britain".

ABF predicts Primark's UK sales will grow by about 1% in the fourth quarter of the year. But like-for-like sales - a key metric in the retail industry, which strips out the impact of store openings and closures - are expected to be "broadly flat" in the UK, and fall 3% across its global operations.

It said sales of autumn/winter clothing started later than normal due to the hot weather in the summer, but "trading was stronger when the weather cooled towards the end of the quarter".

The fast-fashion chain is struggling to compete with brands such as Shein and Boohoo, as well as alternative platforms such as TikTok Shop and Vinted, and in July said it was lowering prices on hundreds of clothing items.

Retail analyst Julie Palmer said that "Primark has been playing catch up for years" and launching home deliveries "is as much about defence as growth".

She told BBC News that "the real test" for the brand is whether it can make home deliveries profitable at the low prices customers have come to expect from fast fashion chains.

"Shein and Vinted have already reset customer expectations on convenience," she said, adding that a "slick and effective returns policy" will also be key.

ABF is planning to spin off Primark from its food business next year.

News.title: BBC drops Drag Race UK after eight series
News.content:
RuPaul's Drag Race UK is leaving the BBC after eight series, the broadcaster has confirmed.

A spokesperson for the broadcaster said it was facing "very difficult choices" in the face of "significant financial pressures".

The show is currently broadcast on BBC Three and iPlayer. Future series - as well as its spin-off vs The World - will be broadcast on Wow Presents Plus, a streaming platform owned by the production company behind the show.

At its peak, the UK version of the international drag competition averaged at around 1.5 million viewers per episode.

A spokesperson for the BBC said it was "proud [...] of this groundbreaking show" and thanked "RuPaul, World of Wonder and everyone involved, both on and off screen".

Started in 2019, Drag Race UK brought British drag into mainstream entertainment in the UK, and has made household names of drag performers such as La Voix, Danny Beard, and Tia Kofi.

The show sees drag queens compete in a series of challenges to impress judges RuPaul, Michelle Visage, Graham Norton and Alan Carr, and often features big name celebrity guest judges.

It has become a staple of LGBTQ+ culture and has been praised for its portrayal of the distinct style of British drag.

The corporation is currently rolling out plans to make Â£500m of savings, with director-general Matt Brittin previously telling staff "the scale of savings requires tough choices".

A BBC spokesperson said: "As the BBC continues to navigate significant financial pressures and deliver the savings required of us, we have had to make some very difficult choices, none of which have been taken lightly."

Announcing the news on Instagram, Wow Presents Plus said a "new era" of Drag Race UK was on the way.

A new series, Drag Race UK All Stars, which sees previous fan favourites return to compete again, will premiere in Autumn 2027 exclusively on Wow Presents Plus.

BBC News understands the current series of Drag Race UK, which launched in September 2026, will continue to air as normal on BBC Three and appear on iPlayer, and all existing series will continue to be available once the move is complete.

News.title: Prince William, Kane and Shearer in campaign to use sport to prevent suicide
News.content:
The Prince of Wales is launching a scheme that aims to use the influence of sport to help prevent suicides, with the support of sports stars including Harry Kane, Kelly Holmes and Alan Shearer.

"Sport has the ability to reach people who may never walk through the door of a mental healthcare service," Prince William is expected to say at an event at Everton's football ground on Thursday.

"People who may never seek support themselves and may be struggling in silence," the prince will say later.

The On Your Side project wants to give people confidence to start the "difficult conversations" with friends, relations, teammates or colleagues who might be struggling with their mental health.

It aims to use the reach of sport to raise awareness about suicide and to show people the help available in a crisis, with the Football Association, Premier League and Team GB providing support.

Thursday's event will be Prince William's biggest public appearance in the UK since the return of the Duke and Duchess of Sussex.

Earlier this week, he attended the funeral of Norway's King Harald in Oslo and brought his son Prince George to his first day as a boarder at Eton College.

The level of suicide is disproportionately higher among men than women - it's the biggest cause of death for men under the age of 50 in the UK.

"My hope is that every sporting organisation in the country will look at what is being launched today and ask a question: 'What more can we do?' Because the opportunity before us is enormous," Prince William will say.

A film has been made, featuring England football captain Harry Kane and boxer Carl Frampton, talking about the importance of stepping in and offering help if people see someone who seems to be facing mental health problems.

Prince William helps to narrate the video, which aims to tackle the stigma around mental health and suicide, with 7,000 lives being lost to suicide each year in the UK.

The initiative has a practical toolkit, on a free website, for people who are worried or embarrassed about what to say to someone if they have concerns about their wellbeing.

It offers a sports-themed way of approaching the topic, called GOALS, representing G: get ready; O: open the conversation; A: ask the question; L: listen and respond and S: support and signpost.

Alan Shearer, former England football star and TV pundit, described it as "the first suicide prevention toolkit designed for the whole of UK sport".

"You don't have to be an expert. You don't have to have all the answers," said Shearer. "But we can all be better at asking, listening, and helping someone find the right support."

Shearer said it was particularly poignant that the launch would be at Everton, one of the clubs where Gary Speed had played, a friend of Shearer's who died by suicide in 2011.

News.title: Group entered hotel of cricketers mistaken for migrants
News.content:
A group of people reached the hotel floor where members of the Pakistan under-19 cricket team were staying after protesters wrongly believed they were migrants, the Pakistan Cricket Board has said.

About 30 to 40 people congregated at the Marriot Hotel in Cosham, Portsmouth, on Tuesday evening after false rumours circulated that a coach carrying migrants had arrived.

Sumair Syed, chief operating officer of the Pakistan Cricket Board, said the team reported people "knocking on their doors" during the incident, but the players "behaved responsibly and didn't escalate the situation".

Hampshire Police said officers found no offences had been committed, and the crowd dispersed by about 21:00 BST.

The team went on to play a scheduled match the following day, Syed said.

He described the incident as "unfortunate" but said he was in contact with the England and Wales Cricket Board (ECB), which had "assured us that every possible measure should be taken for the security of the escort".

"This is the responsibility of the whole sport to ensure the safety, security and well-being of the visiting team," he said. "They are on it and we are hopeful that nothing of such sort will happen in the future."

News.title: Migraines and acne among five more conditions pharmacists can treat
News.content:
People will be able to go to their local chemist in England this autumn and get on-the-spot treatment for 12 common conditions without going to their GP first.

Pharmacists can already prescribe medication for seven conditions - sore throat, earache, sinusitis, shingles, impetigo, infected bites and urinary tract infections.

Five more - migraines, acne, scabies, ear infections and badly blocked noses - are now also being added to that list.

NHS England said the move was to ease pressure on busy GPs and A&E departments while making sure people could get treatment quickly and conveniently.

After a very hot summer and three of the busiest months on record in A&Es in England, the NHS says it wants to make it as easy as possible for people to get help when they need it for everyday conditions.

Prime Minister Andy Burnham said people were "fed up with the scramble for routine appointments" and wanted help close to home, with no more taking time off work or waiting to get seen.

"For five more common conditions, you'll be able to walk into your local pharmacy and get treated on the spot," he said.

Mr Burnham said families would feel the change, and the plan would give people back "precious time".

The five conditions which can now also be treated via pharmacies are:

low frequency migraines in adults

hay fever or allergic rhinitis in children

ear infections in adults

mild to moderate acne in young people and adults

mild skin infections and scabies

That's in addition to these seven:

sore throat

sinusitis

earache

insect bites

impetigo

shingles

uncomplicated UTIs

Initially, a few hundred chemists will offer treatments for the five new conditions, NHS England says.

There will be a gradual rollout and the service will eventually be available at thousands of community NHS pharmacies across England.

Community pharmacies also offer support with healthy eating, exercise, stopping smoking, monitoring your blood pressure, contraception, flu and Covid vaccinations.

News.title: August joint-hottest month on record as climate change and El Niño drive heat
News.content:
August was the joint-hottest month ever recorded, tying with July 2023, according to the EU's climate service.

The record was driven by a combination of climate change and the rising influence of El NiÃ±o, pushing heat into the atmosphere across the Pacific.

Temperatures for the month were 1.65C above pre-industrial levels - surpassing the critical 1.5C threshold agreed by countries to avoid the worst consequences of climate change.

While a single month above 1.5C does not mean it has been permanently crossed, it shows a trend towards breaching that limit.

The month also capped western Europe's warmest summer, with high temperatures pushing the season past the deadly heat of 2003.

News.title: Police launch criminal investigation into Reform UK donations
News.content:
The Metropolitan Police is carrying out a criminal investigation into Reform UK over allegations it broke foreign funding laws, following a broadcast by Channel 4 News last week.

An undercover reporter recorded two senior Reform aides apparently suggesting a way around electoral law to secure foreign party donations, one of which would have totalled Â£500,000.

The police investigation by the Met's Special Enquiry Team is being folded into an inquiry that has been under way into other donations to the party.

A Reform UK spokesman said the party "denies any wrongdoing and will fully cooperate with the investigation".

"We won't be commenting further while a live investigation is under way."

A Met spokesperson said it had received "a number of reports relating to donations and polling involving a political party", after the film by Channel 4 News and Verbatim Investigations was shown on Thursday evening.

In its statement, the Met Police said: "All allegations under investigation relate to potential offences under the Political Parties, Elections and Referendums Act 2000."

"Detectives continue to liaise closely with the Electoral Commission and Crown Prosecution Service as enquiries progress."

The police spokesperson said detectives were seeking to obtain footage relating to the broadcast.

An Electoral Commission spokesperson said the Channel 4 News report included "serious allegations of wrongdoing", adding: "It is right that these are properly and thoroughly investigated by the police.

"In parallel, we are also considering all relevant information and regulatory steps."

The film overshadowed the party's conference in Birmingham and led to the party losing two key figures - Dan Jukes, chief of staff to the leader Nigel Farage, and James Orr, head of policy.

News.title: UK needs new laws for AI in healthcare, says watchdog
News.content:
The UK needs new regulations for AI products used in the NHS and other healthcare settings, says Britain's industry watchdog.

The Medicines and Healthcare Products Regulatory Agency (MHRA), which regulates all medical devices and licenses treatment drugs in the UK, has published 44 recommendations to update its policies as the use of AI in the sector rises.

The technology will soon be routinely used within the NHS, MHRA chief Lawrence Tallon told the BBC.

"What I would expect is that patients will... increasingly see AI as part of the way that normal NHS healthcare is delivered," he said.

"That should happen in a way that they can maintain their trust and their confidence in what's happening."

The report was compiled by an independent commission and involved input from more than 12,000 people including patients and clinicians.

The recommendations include:

Continuously monitoring AI products and removing them from regulatory approval if they malfunction or become less effective over time

Giving patients the right to know whether AI is involved in their care, and easy access to information about the products involved

The power to penalise the developers of an AI product if it fails to meet required standards

An AI "L plate" system which would make it easier for new AI models to be trialled by healthcare professionals under close supervision

"The medical devices regulatory framework predominantly dates from a period where we were thinking about things like hip replacements and knee replacements, or smaller things like stethoscopes and plasters," Tallon said.

He added while current guidelines may work for simple AI products trained to spot known symptoms on scans, for example, the rules do not apply to more complex models.

"Unlike most of the medical products we're used to regulating, these products continue to change after the point of authorization," he said.

"As new data gets fed in, they learn, they adapt, they drift."

And he acknowledged trying to regulate AI is a global challenge.

"I don't think at this moment in time we can point to a single country, a single regulatory framework, and say that they have absolutely cracked it," he said.

News.title: Funeral for second officer killed in A66 crash to be held
News.content:
The funeral for the second police officer killed in a wrong-way crash while on duty will take place later on Thursday.

PC Tom Clough, 38, died on the A66 in South Bank, near Middlesbrough, in the early hours of 22 August alongside his colleague PC Matthew Blades when a Volkswagen Passat collided with their marked armed police car. The five young men in the Passat also died.

PC Blades' funeral took place in Hartlepool on Wednesday with hundreds of police officers from around the country and members of the community lining the street.

Cleveland Police Federation chair Lauren Somerville said PC Clough's partner had said public support "brought them so much strength".

Officers had been pursuing the Passat seconds before it collided with PC Blades and PC Clough's car on the dual carriageway.

The pair had been looking for the Passat after its cloned registration plates triggered an automated number plate recognition camera, although they were not involved in the pursuit, according to the Independent Office for Police Conduct.

The Passat's occupants - Michael Robert Cahill, 23, Jakub Matusiak, 23, Theo Rae, 17, Makai Saddington, 18, and Cole Robert Worthy, 17 - also died.

News.title: Chaplain settles LGBT sermon unfair dismissal case
News.content:
A chaplain who used a sermon to tell pupils they did not have to believe in "LGBT stuff" has reached a legal agreement with the school that dismissed him.

Rev Bernard Randall was sacked by Trent College in Long Eaton, Derbyshire, in 2019, two months after the sermon. He appealed and his dismissal, external was overturned, but he was later made redundant after refusing reduced hours.

After losing an unfair dismissal claim, his case had been set for a new tribunal over possible bias on the panel that made the ruling, and Trent College was ordered to pay Randall about Â£20,000 in costs, according to a court document.

Advocacy group Christian Concern said a confidential settlement had since been reached.

An employment tribunal heard Randall opposed parts of a programme the school was implementing to try to improve LGBT inclusivity.

Randall told the tribunal he believed elements of the programme - devised by charity Educate and Celebrate - were Marxist, revolutionary, atheist and incompatible with Christian values.

He said some of the terminology within the programme was "ideologically loaded and misleading", and he highlighted phrases such as "sex assigned at birth" and "cisgender".

Randall told the tribunal: "Educate and Celebrate went beyond a neutral stance of inclusivity into the implantation of ideas I consider to be identity politics."

He said he was inspired to write the sermon, delivered in June 2019 to pupils aged between 11 and 17, after he was asked by a sixth-form pupil: "Sir, how come we are told we have to accept all this LGBT stuff in a Christian school?"

Randall included the question within the sermon, which he said concerned school leaders.

He also said, in his sermon: "You do not have to accept the ideas of LGBT activists."

Christian Concern said Randall's sermon reflected the Church of England's teaching on marriage, but it triggered complaints from some pupils, parents and staff members, who said it nearly left them in tears.

Randall was removed from his role as chaplain at the fee-paying boarding school and reported to the government counter-terrorism watchdog Prevent.

The Derby Telegraph reported, external Randall appealed against his dismissal, which was overturned, but he was given a final warning. Trent College then informed Randall it wanted to reduce the chaplaincy role to seven hours, term-time only, which he did not accept and was therefore made redundant.

Kimberly Levaco is not like other girls. This much is obvious from the first time we glimpse the hero of Kimberly Akimbo, lacing up her skates at a small-town New Jersey ice rink. She is on the cusp of her 16th birthday, but you wouldn’t know this by looking: she is played by 66-year-old stage veteran Maria Friedman. Kimberly, we quickly learn, is a teenager with a rare, one-in-fifty-million disease, a genetic disorder similar to the real-world condition progeria, in which her body ages four to five times quicker than it ought to.

As you might imagine, there is an inherent melancholy to David Lindsay-Abaire and Jeanine Tesori’s stage musical, making its UK debut at the Hampstead Theatre after an acclaimed, Tony-winning run stateside. From the very first scene, Kimberly is a sort of doomed figure, a woman coming to the end of her life at the point when it’s meant to be starting. (The life expectancy for people with her condition is 16 years old.) She is surrounded by teenagers wrapped up in the the frivolous concerns of adolescence, and adults – including Buddy (Peter Hannah), her deadbeat, booze-dipped dad, and Patty (Niamh Perry), her scatty, mercurial and heavily pregnant mother – who barely seem to have grown up themselves. Kimberly Akimbo mostly opts to keep things light, treating its premise with a kind of wry humour; if there’s such a thing as breezy morbidity, this show has it.

The parameters of Kimberly’s world are contained within one shapeshifting set, designed by Soutra Gilmour, which rotates 360 degrees to become an ice rink, a high school (evoked by a facade of hallway lockers), a library, and Levaco’s three-story house. A giant animated backdrop, mostly used to resemble a big clock, is the only thing remotely cheap-looking or superfluous; mostly, this is a robustly clever staging, and the scale feels just right in its depiction of a New Jersey town that people are itching to leave.

The cast are strong without exception – among them Gilli Jones as Kimberly’s tuba-playing, anagram-obsessed love interest, and Alice Fearn a tornado-like force as Kimberly’s chaotic criminal aunt, who rumbles into town partway through the first act with a harebrained get-rich-quick scheme. It’s Friedman, though, who’s most impressive, ably mimicking the physicality of a teenage girl with a sincerity that evades caricature; it’s the sort of role that is almost never available for older actors, and she makes it look natural. At 66, her voice remains a thing of power and clarity.

Shows like this often live and die by the music, and there is much to enjoy about Tesori’s score, and Lindsay-Abaire’s lyrics, which are never really intricate (beyond the odd internal rhyme) or profound, but consistently lively and well-judged. The music is a cut above most modern musicals, tempering the sort of bright, generically popish sound of its bigger numbers with more classical musical-theatre forms elsewhere.

open image in gallery The company of 'Kimberly Akimbo' ( Marc Brenner )

The question, with imports like Kimberly Akimbo, is whether they will be able to charm British audiences in the same way they did Americans: will a joke about the ignominy of being a Bruce Springsteen hater in New Jersey carry over to North London? Ultimately, the show keeps things broad. This is not a musical about New Jersey at all, or about an ultra-rare genetic malfunction that only a handful of people will ever have to deal with. It is a show about aging, and about youth – those most thoroughly universal of experiences. And in this, it is a clear success.

‘Kimberly Akimbo’ is at the Hampstead Theatre until 7 November

Yemen is moving closer to a return to civil war. The escalating events in the Arab world's poorest country are closely linked to the war in Iran and global efforts to ship oil out of the Gulf region.

Here’s a look at an emerging conflict involving an Iranian-backed rebel group's efforts to keep neighboring Saudi Arabia from using a crucial shipping alternative to the Strait of Hormuz, and how that could tear Yemen apart once more.

What’s happening could return Yemen to civil war

Yemen is home to over 40 million people who fear a return to the civil war that killed 150,000 and brought many others to the brink of famine in one of the world’s most sprawling humanitarian crises. A ceasefire with Yemen’s internationally recognized government and a wider coalition backed by the Saudis began in 2022.

Now that truce is buckling.

Yemen's troubles are in part because of its strategic location at the southern tip of the Arabian Peninsula and alongside the Bab el-Mandeb Strait at the southern end of the Red Sea. It's one of the world's busiest shipping lanes and one that the world is turning to as Iran continues to target ships on the Strait of Hormuz.

The civil war left many Yemenis hungry and beyond the reach of aid. Residents said Thursday the Houthis have now entered the key Red Sea port of Mokha, which has been held by Yemen’s internationally recognized government. If confirmed, that endangers another crucial entry point for food and other assistance.

If the Houthis take Mokha, that’s also one more step toward the Bab el-Mandeb, creating further complications for shipping on the Red Sea — and not only for the Saudis.

The Houthis’ grievance with the Saudis could affect global oil

The ceasefire’s fragile calm held until weeks ago, when the Houthis tested a Saudi-led blockade of rebel-held areas. The Saudis struck the international airport in the rebel-held capital, Sanaa, which the Houthis called an attempt to prevent a plane carrying Houthi leaders from returning home after attending the funeral of Iran’s late supreme leader Ayatollah Ali Khamenei.

The Houthis already objected to the Saudis' backing of Yemeni government forces, who the rebels say have been pounding them this week with dozens of airstrikes after the rebels attacked several oil facilities and utilities in Saudi Arabia, wounding dozens of people.

Now, with the Iran war choking the Strait of Hormuz, the Houthis have a new way to inflict pain on their neighbor by declaring a blockade against Saudi Arabia and targeting its efforts to ship its oil via the Red Sea.

The Houthis' backer, Tehran, doesn’t object to causing the U.S.-allied Saudis pain as it tries to limit oil shipments from the Gulf in service of its war aims.

The Houthis have been relatively unscathed by the recent war

Among Iran’s armed proxies in the region, the Houthis have had a lower profile than Hezbollah in Lebanon and Hamas in Gaza. That, as well as their relative distance, has helped shield them from Israeli attack in the nearly three years since the war in Gaza began.

But the Houthis were quickly targeted with U.S. airstrikes when they tried to insert themselves into the regional conflict by targeting what they called Israeli-linked shipping on the Red Sea off Yemen’s west coast. Those attacks soon faded.

Now, the Houthis are back with a different target, aiming at ships and other assets of Saudi Arabia as it seeks to get its oil out to the world via the Red Sea and the Bab el-Mandeb strait. That Red Sea corridor usually sees $1 trillion of goods move through it per year.

The Houthis are “no longer just positioned on the northern part of the western coast; they now control a much larger stretch of the coastline, bringing them closer to the areas around Bab al-Mandeb,” said Ahmed Nagi, a senior analyst on Yemen at the International Crisis Group.

For global oil consumers already worried about Iran’s attacks on vessels trying to transit the Strait of Hormuz, the threat to yet another global shipping lane is a flashing danger sign, especially with the price of crude oil again trading above $100 a barrel.

___

Anna reported from Jerusalem. Ahmed Haj in Aden, Yemen, contributed.

California has long been farm country, and its oceans soon could be, too.

State coastal officials voted Wednesday to allow a plan to build the United States' largest kelp farm 6 miles (10 kilometers) off the Southern California coast to move forward as the Trump administration seeks to ramp up aquaculture in the Pacific Ocean.

Ocean Rainforest, which is based in the Faroe Islands in Northern Europe, is planning to grow giant kelp on a roughly 3-square-mile (7.8-square-kilometer) stretch of federal waters to develop products to boost soil and plant health in California’s avocado farms and strawberry fields. Some environmentalists are concerned that the lines used to grow seaweed could tangle whales and that increased boat traffic will disrupt an expanse of ocean that has been wild.

Ocean Rainforest said it plans to gradually build up the sea farm over a decade and could harvest as much as 6,000 tons of kelp at full capacity, ramping up a U.S. seaweed industry that lags behind Asia despite the country's extensive coastlines. The plan is to harvest kelp and process it in the port city of Ventura about 60 miles (97 kilometers) northwest of Los Angeles.

“Let’s start in our backyard,” Douglas Bush, Ocean Rainforest's director of California operations, said in a recent interview. “Let’s grow the seaweed here, let’s process here in California, let’s use it in California farms.”

Farm part of push for aquaculture

The proposal to grow kelp off Ventura County comes as the Trump administration seeks to promote commercial aquaculture. The National Oceanic and Atmospheric Administration last year designated 13 areas totaling 33 square miles (85 square kilometers) for the development of aquaculture off California and Texas. The plan is part of a 2020 push to develop the U.S. seafood industry.

It also comes as the market for seaweed has been growing for uses ranging from restaurant dishes to pet food. Dozens of farms are cultivating different types of seaweed in New England, the Pacific Northwest and Alaska. A World Bank report in 2023 estimated seaweed markets could grow another $11.8 billion by 2030.

Some environmental groups backed the California project, noting seaweed can help absorb carbon dioxide from warming ocean waters and restore habitat while feeding off ocean nutrients.

Environmentalists raise questions

But some raised questions about the impact of hundreds of boat trips a year to maintain and harvest the seaweed and the potential for whales migrating or feeding in the area to get tangled in lines stretching up from the sea floor, or tethered to buoys, to grow the kelp. Ocean Rainforest said no whales got tangled in taut lines during a two-year demo project.

“This is our blue Serengeti. This is a very wild place,” said Geoff Shester, director of fishery innovation at the ocean conservation group Oceana. “It’s like you might as well put a bunch of industrial data centers in Yosemite National Park.”

Cassidy Teufel, deputy director at the coastal commission, said during a review of the project that seaweed farms use taut, rigid lines, not the loose fishing lines that are a leading cause of whale entanglements. The farm will be located further offshore where there's a lower density of marine mammals, Teufel said.

It is possible the project will draw fish, and sportfishing will be permitted in the area, Teufel said. Some commercial fishing will be displaced, and Ocean Rainforest and fishermen said they are working on an industry support fund.

Under U.S. law, California officials have a say over projects built on federal properties that will affect the state’s coast. The California Coastal Commission voted unanimously to let the kelp farm move forward with conditions including a phased approach. Ocean Rainforest will initially build in a smaller area and face periodic reviews by the U.S. Army Corps of Engineers and the commission's director before expanding to full capacity.

With the decision, Ocean Rainforest said it has the major approvals needed for the project. Construction could begin in 2027.

The region around Ventura is known for growing strawberries, avocados and other crops.

Ted Travers, chief operating officer of the avocado farm Simpatica, said he was eager to see kelp-based products for agriculture developed on the West Coast. He said in a letter to the commission that all the kelp currently used for agricultural purposes comes from the Atlantic Ocean, “which is financially and environmentally impractical.”

Ventura and port officials welcomed the project as a way to bring new industry and jobs to the city of 100,000 people.

Ryan Giggs has revealed that Manchester United declined the chance to pursue Kylian Mbappe in 2015 having been left unimpressed after a scouting tip.

Giggs had moved on to the coaching staff at Old Trafford under Louis van Gaal after concluding his playing career, and was advised that the club should look at a youngster who then played for Monaco.

“So, I'm in the south of France. I was coaching United, so it'd be 2015. I've been for a walk in the local village and I'm walking back to the hotel. I'm walking on the beach back to the hotel. And you can feel, I can feel someone, you know, when you feel someone like following you," Giggs explained on the Rio Ferdinand Presents podcast.

"And I'm like, I get to the hotel and then all of a sudden I can feel someone coming up to me. Anyway, this guy is called Lionel, French guy. So he comes up to me and says 'hi, I'm Lionel. I just wanted to just say hello. I'm a big United fan and big fan of yours. But I watch a lot of youth football in France, and you have to look at this player. He's called Kylian Mbappé. He's at Monaco and I think he's a player for Man United.'

"A few weeks later, he emailed me all the details. So me and Albert [Stuivenberg] again, who's the coach with Arsenal, he was another assistant at United at the time. We used to in the afternoons just go and watch games or go and watch players at the training ground. So anyway, I've told him about this thing. He says 'come on, let's get him up.' And we got a few youth games with Monaco and we seen him and just like, 'wow, what is this?' You know, you can see players and they can be special, but he did look exceptional, obviously.

"So anyway, we told the scouting team. They went to watch him. Someone in France went to watch him and he was actually playing PSG. Monaco were playing PSG. So they went to Paris to watch him. Anyway, I think a few weeks later, I said to this guy 'how did it go?' and he went 'yeah, they weren't too sure about him, so we just left it, and that was it.'"

Mbappe soon made his senior breakthrough at Monaco, helping the club to the Ligue 1 title in 2017 before joining Paris Saint-Germain for the second highest transfer fee of all time and firing France to World Cup glory. He left PSG for Real Madrid in 2024.

World number two Luke Humphries has insisted his remarkable rise in darts would never have been possible without speaking openly about his mental health struggles.

Humphries, who partnered with the Samaritans to mark World Suicide Prevention Day, was competing on the PDC Tour when an anxiety attack struck midway through a 2019 tournament, leaving him considering retirement.

But talking publicly about his difficulties had a positive impact, driving a surge to the summit of the sport that culminated in winning the 2024 World Championship title and becoming world number one.

"For me, the best thing I ever did was go and see a doctor and go and tell him my feelings. Look who I am now, I’ve achieved so much from doing that and I’m so glad I did," Humphries said in conversation with a Samaritans volunteer.

"The first step is to be open and honest about it, you know when I told my mum and dad stuff, they were really helpful and stuff, helping me get where I needed to be.

open image in gallery Humphries won a world title and became the best player in the world after speaking out (Bradley Collyer/PA) ( PA Wire )

"With what I was going through and the way I was feeling, where I thought my career was going to go, to end up with, four or five years later, with nine major titles, and a World Championship and a World Cup and a Matchplay, I would never have thought that was going to happen to me.

"I thought that would have been impossible because of the way I was feeling at the time.

"I just felt like my career was going to end and I almost thought about giving it up because the stress was playing on me a lot. I decided to stick with it and it was the best choice I ever made, to be honest. It really did pay its dividends."

Data from the Samaritans indicates one in four people experience suicidal thoughts, with suicide standing as the biggest killer of men under 50.

Humphries revealed he still experiences bouts of anxiety, but now understands how to manage them.

"I still get those moments of anxiety and stuff, but they’re just random," he said.

"They’re not in moments you would expect, surrounded by hundreds of people. It could just be a random moment when I’m driving in the car by myself and you just get this bout of anxiety.

"It’s strange, but I know how to deal with it better. You don’t spiral, I think that’s the most important thing. That’s why I feel my mental health has been so much better in the last three to four years."

If you are experiencing feelings of distress, or are struggling to cope, you can speak to the Samaritans, in confidence, on 116 123 (UK and ROI), or visit the Samaritans website to find details of your nearest branch.

If you are based in the USA, and you or someone you know needs mental health assistance right now, call or text 988, or visit 988lifeline.org to access online chat from the 988 Suicide and Crisis Lifeline. This is a free, confidential crisis hotline that is available to everyone 24 hours a day, seven days a week.

If you are in another country, you can go to www.befrienders.org to find a helpline near you.

Flight passengers at Gatwick airport could face further disruption next week as more than 220 assisted travel workers plan to strike over pay.

The walkout was announced by trade union Unite on Wednesday, the day after around 1,300 flights UK flights were grounded following a technical issue with air traffic control systems.

Thousands of passengers, including those flying from Gatwick airport, saw their flights cancelled or delayed.

The industrial action will take place from 17 September to 21 September, then 23 September to 26 September.

Unite has been in negotiations with the workers’ employer, aviation service provider Wilson James, since May.

Union members have unanimously rejected a two-year offer of a 3.4 per cent pay increase, a 0.6 per cent non-consolidated bonus and a 0.5 per cent uplift in pensions.

The union says that this offer “does not go far enough to address years of low pay at the firm”.

It claimed that the lowest-paid members at Wilson James recieve £14.71 per hour while living in an area with a high cost of living. Meanwhile, its highest-paid director received a 38.7 per cent pay rise last year.

Unite regional officer Ben Davis said: “Unite has been trying to negotiate a better pay deal for our members for months, however Wilson James has failed to put forward an offer that is acceptable to workers.

“Industrial action will inevitably disrupt services throughout Gatwick, but this is a direct result of Wilson James refusal to make a fair offer to our members. Strikes can be avoided, but that requires the company making a significantly improved offer.”

In a statement, Gatwick airport commented: “We are working with our assisted travel provider, Wilson James, to avoid any impacts and we expect to operate a normal flight schedule for our airlines and passengers on these dates.

“Of course, we hope Wilson James and their union can reach a resolution before then."

The Independent has contacted Wilson James for comment.

News.title: Grandfather escapes trial after 16 ‘feral’ children rescued from Ohio house of horrors
News.content:

An Ohio grandfather accused of keeping 16 of his grandchildren trapped in a filth-ridden 'house of horrors' has been declared mentally unfit to face trial over the horrific neglect.

A judge in Vinton County accepted the findings of an official evaluation for 73-year-old Gary Siders Sr. on Wednesday. Prosecutor William Archer raised no objections to the report. Siders appeared in court in a wheelchair, while his attorney, Dorian Baum, revealed his client's declining mental state has been worsening for years and is 'not restorable.'

'It’s not really a surprise to any of us that he’s not been found competent at this point,' Baum said following the hearing. 'He doesn’t fully understand or appreciate what’s going on.'

open image in gallery A judge in Vinton County accepted the findings of an evaluation report for Gary Siders Sr. Vinton County Prosecutor William Archer did not object to the findings

The elderly man faced 16 counts of child endangerment over the treatment of the children, who were rescued on June 30 from a squalid property in Hamden, located about 80 miles south of Columbus.

When law enforcement officers breached the home, they uncovered what Vinton County Sheriff Ryan Cain described as a 'disgusting scene.' The 16 children—ranging in age from just 18 months to 18 years old—were routinely confined inside a tiny, 12-by-12-foot space littered with an 'extremely high presence' of human feces.

When asked by reporters whether the isolated youths were literate, Ohio Attorney General Andy Wilson painted a tragic picture, stating the children looked 'almost like feral animals' and that several 'couldn't even speak.'

open image in gallery Investigators said the children remained mostly confined to a small room in the house under deplorable conditions ( Copyright 2026 The Associated Press. All rights reserved )

Surrounding neighbors reported that they had never once seen the kids outdoors over two decades. None of the victims were enrolled in school.

The shocking discovery came despite child protective services investigating the family years earlier. Records show that Gallia County Children's Services opened an inquiry in March 2020 after educators at the online Ohio Virtual Academy raised alarms over severe educational neglect.

Teachers reported that an 11-year-old Siders child could not write the alphabet, could not pronounce any letter sounds, and could only count to 12. A 13-year-old sibling had completely dropped out after failing to submit work for an entire month. The parents continuously ignored requests to schedule required medical examinations and speech therapy sessions for the children.

open image in gallery The children weren’t enrolled in school, the family moved around over the past two decades, and neighbors said they’d never spotted the kids ( AP )

By December 2020, a local physician alerted county officials that the parents were skipping vital follow-up medical visits, warning that the kids were at risk of severe developmental delays linked to potential lead poisoning.

During a home visit, a caseworker found roaches, gnats, and flies swarming the residence, along with two children with visible insect bites and bruising. Despite the appalling conditions, Gallia County Children’s Services permitted the parents to retain physical custody, placing the family under protective supervision in January 2021 before closing the file five months later after claiming the parents had satisfied a court-approved case plan.

The children’s father, Gary Siders Jr., 36, mother Elizabeth Siders, 33, and grandmother Christina Siders, 68, have all pleaded not guilty to 19 counts of child endangerment each.

open image in gallery Siders’ wife, Christina Siders; son Gary Siders Jr., and daughter-in-law, Elizabeth Siders, the children’s mother, have pleaded not guilty ( AP )

Defending the patriarch before his competency ruling, attorney Dorian Baum claimed the house was fully functional with working utilities and food, telling local reporters that critics should 'step back' from what he argued was a state agency 'criminalizing poverty.'

However, the horror runs even deeper. The initial search warrant that led deputies to discover the captive children was actually executed as part of a separate sex crimes investigation. In that case, both Gary Siders Jr. and Elizabeth Siders face counts of sexual battery and unlawful sexual conduct with a minor involving a child outside their immediate family.

All 16 rescued children were hospitalized for evaluation before being transferred into state protective custody.

The UK is bracing for a wet and windy start to the weekend before conditions settle into sunnier spells for most on Sunday.

The rain is set to offer a welcome change of pace following Met Office confirmation that summer 2026 was the UK’s hottest on record.

The average mean temperature between June and August reached a historic 16.5C, breaking the previous record set only last year.

Now, temperatures are expected to cool over the weekend, dropping to between 13C and 16C.

open image in gallery Temperatures are expected to drop this weekend ( Met Office )

Met Office spokesperson Nicola Maxey explained: “Conditions are expected to turn more unsettled through the weekend as weather systems move in from the Atlantic.

“Saturday will see a band of rain move southeast across the UK, bringing some wet and locally windy conditions at times, particularly across northern and western areas.”

Tracking eastwards, these weekend showers are expected to move across the Midlands, Scotland, Northern Ireland, Wales and East Anglia, before the start of a sunnier spell on Sunday.

But the wetter weather will not bring an end to drought in the country, experts have cautioned.

Prolonged heatwaves and dry stretches over the Summer left large parts of England and Wales in drought conditions — parching agricultural soils, depleting reservoirs, and prompting hosepipe bans.

open image in gallery More rain will be needed to bring an end to prolonged dry conditions ( Getty )

At the peak of the August heatwave, almost three quarters of the UK were experiencing drought. The Environment Agency’s latest report indicates that there has been little change so far.

While rain over the weekend will help moisten topsoils, more significant and sustained winter downpours will be needed to replenish groundwater levels.

In the days ahead, forecasters expect a classic autumn mix of rain, wind, and sunshine as weather fronts sweep in from the west.

Scotland

Brisk winds and rain move across the region today, turning showery in the northwest later. After a finer Friday with showers mostly confined to the morning, Saturday brings a return of wet and windy conditions before drier weather arrives on Sunday.

Northern England

Rain and gusty breezes sweep eastward across the region today before clearing overnight to leave fine, sunny spells for Friday. Saturday sees another band of wet, windy weather push through, yielding to sunshine and scattered showers by Sunday.

Wales

Persistent rain clears eastwards overnight, paving the way for a bright Friday with pleasantly warm sunshine. A blustery wet front moves southeastward across the country on Saturday, clearing in time for a drier and calmer Sunday.

Southern England

Cloud builds today with patchy rain developing, but skies clear overnight. Friday will feel pleasantly warm with sunny spells. While Saturday night brings a spell of rain and wind, Sunday will offer the best of the weekend's dry, bright weather.

Northern Ireland

Brisk winds and heavy morning rain gradually give way to showery outbreaks in the west. Friday offers fine, dry weather before fresh Atlantic rain and winds arrive on Saturday, clearing to sunshine and showers on Sunday.

News.title: Mosquitoes are evolving to evade bed nets – but there may be a solution
News.content:
In Papua’s low-lying mangrove swamps and dense tropical rainforests, mosquitoes have always got to work early.

Here, the disease-ridden insects begin feeding in the early evening as people socialise and children play. It’s a characteristic that’s hampered malaria control efforts, because it has rendered bed nets less effective. People are bitten before they climb under the netting to sleep.

It’s also part of the reason that Indonesian Papua remains one of Asia’s most persistent malaria hotspots. Last year, cases across the country jumped by 30 per cent, to 706,000 new infections. The vast majority, roughly 90 per cent, were reported in Papua’s six provinces.

The same pattern is now emerging in parts of sub-Saharan Africa, where mosquitoes used to bite mostly at night and where the rollout of insecticide-treated bed nets is estimated to have averted 450 million malaria cases between 2000 and 2015, according to modelling in Nature journal.

A number of studies suggest mosquitoes in Africa are evolving in response to the mass rollout of bed nets, biting earlier in the evening, or later in the morning. In some cases, species which already did this have become more dominant, while others are adapting their habits.

“We’re battling evolution. And right now, we’re losing,” said Prof Neil Lobo, a research professor in the Eck Institute for Global Health at the University of Notre Dame.

“Mosquitoes are adapting. They’re biting outdoors, they’re biting earlier in the evening when people aren’t under their nets, and they’re becoming resistant to the insecticides we use. So we’re reaching the limits of what bed nets alone can do,” he told The Telegraph.

But there may be a solution.

News.title: Palmer and Rogers complete 12-minute rescue mission to save Chelsea
News.content:
Xabi Alonso needed the cavalry – and referee Jarred Gillett – to stop Chelsea making a quick exit from the Carabao Cup and, boy, did they come up trumps for him.

Chelsea had looked to be heading out of the competition shortly after half-time, but, in Cole Palmer and Morgan Rogers, Alonso has a cheat code that is capable of masking even the worst defending.

Alonso’s side have shared 26 goals in the five games they have played this season. It has certainly been an entertaining start by Chelsea’s latest manager.

Palmer, Rogers and Pedro Neto stepped off the substitutes’ bench to complete a stunning rescue mission against Leeds United. Palmer scored twice, Neto once and Rogers helped himself to at least a hat-trick of assists. He claimed it was four, but the record books may say three.

When it was announced Palmer had been awarded the player of the match, Rogers responded by saying: “Mate, I got four assists. I can’t believe that! That’s mental. He scored a pen!”

News.title: Martin Odegaard bails out comically wasteful Arsenal
News.content:
In five matches this season, Odegaard has already scored four goals. That is three more than he managed in the whole of last season. The Arsenal captain is fit again and he is flowing. As ever, when Odegaard flows, Arsenal flow.

“That’s what we need, the players with that mindset to decide the game and play with that personality,” said Mikel Arteta. “He has got that edge. He’s getting into those positions much more in recent games.”

In the end it was a thoroughly deserved victory for the Premier League side, who were superior to Napoli in every department. Were it not for their comically bad finishing, they would have guaranteed the result long before Odegaard’s 75th-minute strike.

Their expected goals figure suggested they should have scored more than four goals, compared to Napoli’s 0.22. In total, they registered 26 shots – the most of any Arsenal team on record in a single Champions League match, and the most on record a Napoli team has ever faced.

“With the amount of chances we generated, the scoreline has to reflect a very different result,” said Arteta. “The number of players that got into this situation, the amount of situations that we generated in various ways was something that pleased me a lot.”

News.title: Mac Allister not so sad now after Liverpool comeback winner
News.content:
Do your talking on the pitch, as the old adage goes, and Alexis Mac Allister emphatically did just that as Liverpool came from behind to thrillingly win their first Champions League tie under new head coach Andoni Iraola in what was his debut at this level.

On the eve of this encounter, against a strong Atlético Madrid, one of the clubs who have recently tried to sign him, Mac Allister had spoken of his sadness. Sadness that, unlike fellow midfielders Dominik Szoboszlai – Liverpool’s other scorer here – and Ryan Gravenberch, he had not been offered and signed a new contract.

So, earn it. And many more goals – and overall performances like this – there is no doubt the Argentinian will have a deal placed in front of him. He scored with an arresting second-half shot, which proved to be the winner, and the smile across his face said it all. Not so sad now as he was later substituted to a standing ovation with Gravenberch taking his place.

The goal came early in the second half, with Iraola attributing that to adjusting his tactics after being flummoxed by Atlético’s back five and packed midfield in a first half when Liverpool were second best.

Mac Allister was heavily involved through the build-up, eventually picking out Rio Ngumoha on the left whose shot was blocked and pinballed around. It dropped to Mac Allister, 20 yards out, and he hit the kind of unerring drive that gives the goalkeeper no chance. And so it proved. Boom. And Anfield was bouncing.

News.title: Gay does enough to earn another chance as England dominate again
News.content:
There are two places up for grabs in England’s top three and three players vying: Gay, Jordan Cox and Jacob Bethell, who spent the day on the players’ balcony dropping a reminder of his looming return. A hundred for Durham by Ben McKinney, the one challenger outside of the squad, tweaked the ante up further.

One of Cox or Gay will make way for Bethell when England begin their next series in Johannesburg on December 17, which will be the first Test of the Stephen Fleming era and the first big call he has to make. Cox was on the up after scores of 75 at Headingley and 55 in the first innings at Lord’s, looking the part at No 3. Gay’s luck had run out with a grubber in the second Test and he wasted a couple of 30s in other innings. Cox has opened in first-class cricket and Bethell could also take on the role of Ben Duckett’s partner. The squeeze was on.

But Cox perhaps got a little ahead of himself and played what could be a costly, impetuous shot at Mohammad Abbas to fall for six and hand Gay a chance. Neither Cox nor Gay have been tested on the back foot by genuine pace which will happen at the Wanderers in December but their performances have to be judged against the backdrop of a seam bowlers’ summer. Gay is averaging 27.1 from 10 innings, a number probably worth another 10 runs given the conditions.

His dismissal 20 minutes before the close, playing on driving away from his body, was the one time his footwork was non-existent and Razaullah deserved the breakthrough for coming back and hitting 90mph after tea following so little first-class cricket and a rushed call-up amidst the bloodletting.

News.title: I got a first look at Apple’s new £2k iPhone – it’s not just the price that makes it stand out
News.content:
Apple has entered the foldable phone race with the iPhone Duo, following years of speculation about whether the company would ever bend its famously rigid design philosophy.

Barely a month after Samsung dropped its latest Galaxy Z Fold 8, this is the moment Apple stakes its claim in a category it has avoided for the last decade. I was at the launch event at Apple’s HQ in Cupertino, California for a first look.

Similar in size to a British passport, the new smartphone unfolds like a miniature book to reveal a large 7.6-inch inner screen. When closed, it’s shorter and wider than a traditional iPhone, and when opened, it resembles a small iPad.

What makes the iPhone Duo worth your attention isn’t just that it’s the first hinged phone with an Apple logo, but that it addresses some of the biggest frustrations currently plaguing folding mobiles.

You can barely see the crease on the inner display, and it doesn’t look like a cheap plastic sheet. It’s intuitive to use, and fully waterproof, which is rare among rivals. Whether all that justifies a £2,000 price tag, however, is another question entirely.

News.title: Man City survive tunnel clash and Porto fury thanks to Haaland double
News.content:
Enzo Maresca takes charge of his first Champions League game in charge of Manchester City as they have travelled to Portugal to take on Porto at the Estadio do Dragao. These sides last met during the Champions League group stages during the 2020/21 season. Manchester City won 3-1 at home before the two sides drew 0-0 in this stadium.

Manchester City were busy late on in the transfer window, bringing in both Iliman Ndiaye and Enzo Fernandez as they spent nearly £200m on deadline day alone. They come into tonight’s game off the back of three straight Premier League victories to kick off the Maresca era. Maresca has limited Champions League experience as a manager, which came with Chelsea last season. Manchester City have won their opening game of a Champions League campaign in six of the last seven seasons but this will be the first time since 2015/16 that Manchester City embark on a Champions League campaign without Pep Guardiola at the helm.

“It is a hard place to come [Porto],” said Maresca. “They have started really well. In the last 14/15 games in Europe they lost just one, that shows a difficult place to come, but we will try our best and try to win the game. It is a very, very good team. They have different players, but in terms of the team it is very clear in the way they play. They are aggressive without the ball and on the ball, they have a clear style. But we will try our best and try to win the game. The ambition is the same; try to be ourselves and to win games and then we will see.”

Porto, managed by Francesco Farioli, have won every league game so far this season and already sit four points clear at the summit of Liga Portugal. Farioli takes charge of his first game as a manger in the Champions League and the club make their return to the elite European competition after two seasons away.

“We are going to face one of the big favourites to win the competition,” Farioli said. “It will be a game that will demand that we be at our best, and we know that whenever we step onto the Dragão pitch, something special can happen. I am happy to be in the Champions League for the first time at 37 years old. This will be my first game, but we approach every game with the same attention to detail and the same focus. It is easy for the players to be motivated tomorrow [tonight]. But the key will be our strategy and our ability to execute it, individually and collectively.”

Porto were in the Europa League last season, making it to the quarter-finals, where they were knocked out by Nottingham Forest 2-1 on aggregate. The omens would not appear to be on Porto’s side tonight; they have only won two of their last 16 games against English opposition in major European competition.

Team news from Portugal to follow shortly.

Sports.content:

Mikel Arteta’s side enter the competition at this late stage due to their participation in the Champions League.

Sports.title: Man Utd make major change to kit for Champions League return after three years away as Carrick prepares for Sabah test
Sports.content:
MANCHESTER UNITED Foundation will be spotlighted on the team’s kit throughout the Champions League campaign.

United return to Europe’s elite competition tonight when they host debutants Sabah at Old Trafford after a three-year absence.



And Man Utd announced the charity’s logo will be featured on the back of the men’s team’s shirts for all Champions League games.

The Foundation was stablished in 2007 and works with over 30,000 young people each year.



It delivers 129 projects providing educational and community engagement programmes to help young participants make positive choices in their lives.

Manchester United Foundation CEO Ashley Hackett stated that putting the charity in the spotlight at top level will help drive awareness of all the life-changing work in the local community.



Hackett said: “This is a wonderful opportunity for us, offering unparalleled exposure on one of football’s biggest stages during Manchester United‘s famous European nights.

“We’re incredibly proud of the vital work we do to support young people from communities across Greater Manchester, where our impact is genuinely life changing.

“Proceeds generated from this initiative will be instrumental in helping us to continue to deliver our programmes that make a huge difference to those we work with.

“On behalf of everyone at the Foundation, I’d like to thank the club for this fantastic support.”



BEST ONLINE CASINOS – TOP SITES IN THE UK

United fans will soon be able to support the initiative by visiting the club’s Megastore and have the logo printed onto their new or existing shirt.

Net profits will be donated to the Foundation to support its work with young people across Greater Manchester and beyond.

Michael Carrick‘s side will also face Bayern Munich, RB Leipzig, Roma, Atletico Madrid, Como, Sporting Lisbon and Villarreal in the league phase of this season’s Champions League.

Sports.title: Jill Scott lands shock job at SALFORD as former Man Utd kit sponsors pour money into club as minority equity investors
Sports.content:
LIONESSES icon Jill Scott has joined Salford City as chief advisor to the women’s team.

Members of the Class of ’92 including Ryan Giggs, Paul Scholes, David Beckham and Gary Neville took part-ownership of Salford City in 2014.



High-profile backing took the Salford men’s team from the eighth-tier of English football to League Two, where they have played for the past eight seasons.

Beckham and Neville are the only Manchester United legends who remain in an ownership capacity, with Scholes sticking around to oversee recruitment.



And now another famous face has been added to the mix.

Scott, 39, starred for the likes of Everton, Manchester City and England before forging a successful career in media and television.



The former I’m A Celeb winner is a regular on the Stick to Football podcast with Neville, who she will now link up with at Salford.

The club say Scott will “play a key role in shaping the technical programme for the Salford City Lionesses and Academy teams while supporting the development of players and coaching staff.”

United’s former shirt sponsors, the insurance giants AIG, have also become part of the Salford set-up as the largest minority equity investor in the Lionesses.

The women’s team was formed in 2018 and currently plays in tier five of the women’s football pyramid.

Sports.title: Man Utd vs Man City tickets: Where to buy them and how much do they cost for mega Manchester derby?
Sports.content:
THE Manchester derby is one of the standout fixtures of every Premier League season.

And this year, the bitter rivals meet just four games into the new campaign at Old Trafford.



Manchester United made a disappointing start to the new campaign after a 2-0 opening day defeat to newly promoted Hull.

But Michael Carrick‘s men quickly improved, smashing Ipswich 5-2 before a gut-wrenching 2-2 draw at Everton.

Sports.title: Richarlison ‘could TERMINATE Tottenham deal for shock free transfer to Brazil as he explores legal options after axe’
Sports.content:
RICHARLISON is set to try to terminate his Tottenham contract in a bid to move back to Brazil as a free agent.

The 29-year-old forward is reportedly looking to take legal action against the North London club in an attempt to join Vasco da Gama.



The Spurs star, who joined in 2022, is hoping to link up with Pedro Emanuel’s side – according to Globo Esporte.

The clock is ticking for him to be unregistered from his current side with the Brazilian transfer deadline set for Friday.



Roberto De Zerbi & Co opted not to sign Richarlison up to the first-team, but rather demote him to the under-21s.

Richarlison‘s legal team are battling the legality of removing him from the first-team and looking to annul his entire contract with the Lilywhites.



The transfer window is fairly irrelevant to the termination of his deal because the request has already been notified.

Therefore, Richarlison could still sign for Vasco da Gama, his childhood team, even after the deadline.

A loan was initially considered, but the idea was thrown out due to Fifa regulations.

Meanwhile, Tottenham are demanding a £19.33m fee for their forward – one that Vasco cannot afford.



BEST FREE BETS AND BETTING SIGN UP OFFERS

Richarlison joined Antonio Conte‘s Spurs side in July 2022 in a five-year deal worth £60million from Everton.

The Toffees were under pressure from Premier League Profit and Sustainability rules and were forced to let the star go.

While the Merseyside hierarchy were not overwhelmed by the £60m fee, their hands were tied if they wanted to give then-boss Frank Lampard some wriggle room.

But now, the Brazil international – who earned 54 caps, and scored 20 goals for his nation – could be leaving the capital on a free.



Last year, Renan Lodi had a comparable situation to Richarlison’s current dilemma when he walked out of Al-Hilal.

After reaching an agreement with the club, Lodi unilaterally terminated his contract with the Saudi side.

And eight months later, the 28-year-old signed for Brazil side Atletico Mineiro.

Sports.title: I KO’d Liverpool from FA Cup with minnows & snapped selfie with Nev.. now I’m out to dent Man Utd Champions League dream
Sports.content:
TYMOTEUSZ PUCHACZ has form when it comes to causing a huge upset – and now he is looking to make Manchester United his next victim.

The left-back, 27, is expected to be named in the Sabah side taking on the Red Devils in the Champions League tonight.



The Azerbaijan-based minnows are the ultimate underdogs, with their boss Valdas Dambrauskas previously appearing on Lithuania’s version of Who Wants to Be a Millionaire?

Sabah are competing in the league phase for the first time in their NINE-YEAR history after sealing a stunning comeback win over Hapoel Be’er Sheva in the play-off round.



And Puchacz will be among the shock names aiming to dent United’s Champions League dream.

The Polish star had a loan spell with EFL side Plymouth in 2025, making 18 appearances.

In that time with Argyle, he sensationally dumped United’s arch-rivals Liverpool out of the FA Cup.

Puchacz played the full 90 minutes as Ryan Hardie’s second half penalty steered Plymouth past the Merseyside giants.

The former Panathinaikos man kept the likes of Luis Diaz, Diogo Jota and Federico Chiesa at bay during a memorable day at Home Park.

The defender put his 10km run on hold when he bumped into United icon Gary Neville in Marbella.

He posed for an unexpected selfie with now-Real Madrid right-back Trent Alexander-Arnold.

Sports.title: Premier League club’s stadium expansion plans get major boost with capacity expected to become one of England’s biggest
Sports.content:
NOTTINGHAM Forest’s City Ground is awaiting a huge expansion with a date finally set for a crunch planning committee debate.

In January, plans were submitted to boost the capacity of the historic stadium to around 52,500.



And last week, three local Labour MPs published a joint statement praising the “historic opportunity” to boost the Nottingham economy.

Rushcliffe Borough Council’s planning committee will now meet on September 16 at 6pm to consider the whole application over “at least two hours”.



It has been a long time coming for Forest fans who first heard of plans to expand in 2019.

The argument for expansion struggled to get going until Steve Cooper‘s side secured promotion to the Premier League in 2022.



In June 2025, a green light was given to flatten and rebuild the existing Peter Taylor Stand – taking capacity from about 30,000 to 35,000.

According to the Local Democracy Reporting Service, it was only six months later that even larger ideas surfaced with official documents submitted in January.

Improved plans have been promised as concerns were raised over transport plans.

A borough council spokesperson said they will still “work positively” with Forest to review everything.



BEST FREE BETS AND BETTING SIGN UP OFFERS

Nottingham East MP Nadia Whittome, Nottingham North and Kimberley MP Alex Norris and Nottingham South MP Lilian Greenwood all put their names to the document in support of the Tricky Trees.

Their joint statement read: “This is a historic opportunity to celebrate and preserve our city’s proud heritage as home to a world-famous club.

“While boosting our local economy and creating well-paid, unionised jobs.

“The case for a bigger stadium has been clear for years – six consecutive seasons of sold-out games have meant that many thousands of local fans cannot see their team play on home turf, including a whole new generation of young supporters.

“Greater capacity will enable NFFC to host major international matches in future tournaments, strengthening our visitor economy by firmly putting Nottingham back on the map as a legendary football city.”

Sports.title: ‘You stitched me right up’ – TNT Sports host Olivia Buzaglo left in stitches by Man Utd star Bryan Mbeumo’s cheeky prank
Sports.content:
BRYAN MBEUMO left TNT Sports’ Olivia Buzaglo in stitches after joking about one of his hidden talents.

Buzaglo interviewed the Manchester United winger ahead of the Red Devils’ Champions League opener against Sabah FK tonight.



And in their sit-down, she asked the Cameroon international if the rumours of him being an adept piano player are true.

As their chat drew to a close, she said: “And just finally, I heard you’re into the piano, am I right?”



Mbeumo replied: “Yeah, a bit.”

Buzaglo then asked the former Brentford man if he was able to play the iconic Champions League theme song, which was slightly changed ahead of the 2024-25 season.



She asked: “Can you play the Champions League music on the piano?”

And much to Buzaglo’s amazement, Mbeumo calmly replied: “I can.”

She replied: “Can you actually? Oh my gosh, that’s amazing.

“Where did you learn that?”



SUN VEGAS WELCOME OFFER: GET UP TO £100 BONUS

Mbeumo, however, started to crack up as she expressed her amazement and then admitted: “No, I can’t, that’s a joke.”

Buzaglo said: “Oh my God, you’ve actually stitched me right up. That was very believable.”

Buzaglo then implored the £71million man to learn how to play the theme song.

She said: “Bryan, I think you should learn how to play the Champions League music because that would actually be really cool.”

United’s clash with Sabah will be their first Champions League game in nearly THREE YEARS.



Manager Michael Carrick said: “It’s a magical competition. It’s where we all want to be.

“When you’re out of it, you realise how special it is and when you’re in it, you want to make the most of it.

“I think we’ve all seen some special, special nights and felt some special things in this competition over the years.



“It’s where we want to be, it’s what we want to get back to.

“And it’s the best competition to challenge yourself and to push against the best.

Sports.title: Premier League 'give in to Man Utd' as huge fixture announcement being made TODAY
Sports.content:
Premier League 'give in to Man Utd' as huge fixture announcement being made TODAY

The Premier League are set to announce the December fixtures today, with Manchester United among the clubs who pushed for the earlier release

View Image Manchester United were among the clubs who pushed for the earlier release

The Premier League will release the Christmas fixture schedule today after pressure from clubs including Manchester United. United were among the clubs who asked the league and broadcasters to bring the announcement forward to give supporters more time to plan and reduce disruption.

‌



That push appears to have worked, with the fixtures due to be released more than a month earlier than they were last season. While all matches are initially listed for 3pm on the Saturday, they remain subject to change once broadcasters select their televised games.

‌



According to the Mail, United officials are understood to have met with the Premier League and broadcasters to stress the importance of prioritising supporters, urging that December's fixture decisions be made well in advance. The aim is to make travel planning easier for fans hoping to attend.

‌



The Football Supporters' Association is also believed to have been involved in the discussions. Last season, the festive fixtures were announced on 15 October and United's home game against Newcastle United was the only one scheduled for an 8pm kick‑off on Boxing Day.

This year, Boxing Day falls on a Saturday, and several games are expected to be played on that date. With it being a Saturday, there's a strong possibility that some fixtures will kick off at 3pm.

‌

Sports.title: EFL manager makes outrageous 'volleyed his cat' statement in best interview of the season
Sports.content:
EFL manager makes outrageous 'volleyed his cat' statement in best interview of the season

An EFL manager was inventive when describing a key decision made during a Championship game

View 2 Images An EFL manager made his thoughts clear on a key decision made in a Championship match (Image: Sky Sports)

Charlton Athletic boss Nathan Jones had a bizarre way of describing the linesman’s reaction after seeing a goal disallowed for offside. The Addicks drew 0-0 with Queens Park Rangers at The Valley on Wednesday night.

Both sides have made impressive starts to their Championship campaigns. Charlton headed into the game having picked up 10 points from their first five games, with QPR matching the home side’s tally.

A win for either team could have potentially seen the victor end the night top of the table. However, Charlton were denied all three points after seeing Tyreece Campbell's first half effort disallowed for an offside call in the first half.

While the game ended goalless, the match was not short of talking points. Charlton boss Jones did not hold back as he slammed the assistant referee’s decision in a box office interview and blamed officials for his side dropping points.

Get YOUR Mirror Football Newsletter Get our comprehensive football coverage, with news, updates, opinions, analysis and everything that matters to you, straight to your inbox. To get it, it's a quick and easy one-two: 1. Head THIS WAY 2. Enter your email and hit Subscribe

“They were giving offsides willy-nilly because we had one in the second half that wasn’t and the goal is a great goal,” Jones told Sky Sports. “It’s a great ball, it’s a great counter-attack, it’s onside and it’s cost us three points. That’s cost us three points once again.

“And the arrogance of the linesman is mental because he’s like looking at me as if I’ve just volleyed his cat! He is looking at me as if I have done something and going, ‘Nah.’

“The biggest error of the night and he’s cost us the game and that is the Championship. Because the Championship is brutal, these are a good side, we’re competing with monsters.”

View 2 Images Tyreece Campbell saw his goal disallowed for Charlton against QPR (Image: Charlotte Wilson/Offside/Offside via Getty Images)

JOIN US ON FACEBOOK! Latest news, analysis and much more on Mirror Football's Facebook page

Jones also made it clear that he had been unhappy with the decisions made in Charlton’s previous game. The club lost 4-0 to Stoke City last weekend, going behind to an early Justin Devenny penalty and seeing Danny McNamara sent off shortly after the interval. The ruling out of Campbell’s goal against QPR appeared to compound the manager’s frustration with officials.

“We scored the only goal of the game and once again, I’m sick of it,” Jones said. “Honestly, I’m sick of it. On the weekend, I had to put up with a performance from an individual that was…I want to use adjectives but I can’t because I’ll get in trouble…that was beyond the realms of belief.”

Charlton will hope to get back to winning ways against Portsmouth on Saturday. Meanwhile, QPR are set for a tough trip to current league leaders West Bromwich Albion this weekend.

Sports.title: Mikel Arteta spotted 'raging' at three Arsenal stars during Napoli win
Sports.content:
Mikel Arteta spotted 'raging' at three Arsenal stars during Napoli win

Arsenal secured a narrow win at Napoli on Wednesday night and, as they attempted to see out the game, Mikel Arteta lamented three of his players for not tracking back

View 2 Images Mikel Arteta saw Arsenal keep up their percent start to the season

Mikel Arteta was seen letting rip at three of his attacking players during Arsenal's win over Napoli - demanding that they work off the ball.

‌



The Gunners kept up their perfect start to the season after winning in Naples, owing to Martin Odegaard's strike on 75 minutes. The Premier League champions though were wasteful throughout as they spurned numerous chances.

‌



After missing one that would've made it 2-0, Arteta felt that Kai Havertz, Noni Madueke and Christos Tzolis weren't tracking back as Napoli countered in an attempt to score a late equaliser.

‌



The Arsenal boss blasted the trio, demanding that they get back into position, which was spotted by TNT Sports co-commentator Lucy Ward.

She said: "Mikel Arteta was absolutely raging on the sidelines that Havertz, Madueke and Tzolis weren’t recovering after that attack. It was so interesting. As the Arsenal attack finished, those three all sort of ambled back, and Mikel Arteta ran down the sidelines and shouted at them to recover."

Arsenal were able to hold out as they secured victory in what will be one of their more challenging away days in the Champions League. Although they do still face a daunting trip to Bayern Munich later in the tournament.

Arteta was full of praise for how his side performed and felt the narrow margin of victory didn't highlight how dominant they were, but admitted that they were wasteful in front of goal.

‌

He said after the game: "We fully deserved the three points. The performance probably doesn’t reflect the result, the team was superb. We showed quality in a lot of moments to break them down and it was a shame because we missed so many great chances.

"On any other day the result would be different. We should have done it in a different way because of the amount of chances we created but we got the win in the end."
