Demirovic quickly re-established the lead ​in the ​26th minute and then completed ​the hat-trick with a hooked volley six minutes later. “For me personally it was the perfect start and also for the team as a whole,” Demirovic told Dazn.

Quick Guide Championship: Ten-man West Brom win at Derby to go top Show West Bromwich Albion held on for a memorable 1-0 victory over Derby at Pride Park, after playing for more than an hour with 10 men. Aune Heggebø's early goal proved enough to take the Baggies top of the table, despite Brayann Pereira being dismissed on his debut after collecting two first-half yellow cards. Derby had started the stronger, but West Brom swept downfield to score in the 16th minute, Jimmy-Jay Morgan whipping in a low cross from the left which Heggebø [pictured] finished at the near post. The visitors were rocked by the dismissal of Pereira in the 34th minute, as he was shown a second yellow card for a clumsy challenge on Charlie Taylor. The hosts went close just before half-time when David Ozoh flashed a low ball across the six-yard box with no white shirt able to turn it in. Derby should have levelled in the 68th minute but Lars-Jørgen Salvesen headed over from Joe Ward’s cross. Late on, Nat Phillips made a great clearance after a late goalmouth scramble, summing up a performance full of grit and resolve. James Morrison's side move above West Ham to top the Championship table with 13 points from six games. Either Charlton or QPR could have joined them on 13 points, but the sides played out a stalemate at the Valley. Derby, meanwhile, slipped into the bottom three with their fourth defeat in six games. Norwich moved up to ninth in the table as they edged past visitors Birmingham 2-1 to make it three wins in four league games. Oscar Schwartau's screamer opened the scoring, the young Dane lashing an unstoppable right-footed drive past James Beadle from 25 yards out. Papa Diallo's first goal for the Canaries doubled their advantage before the break, as the Senegal winger sidefooted home from Andre Brooks' cross. Carlos Vicente pulled a goal back for the visitors, but wasted a glorious chance to equalise near the end as Chris Davies’ men suffered their first league defeat this season. Press Association Photograph: Morgan Harlow/Getty Images Europe Was this helpful? Thank you for your feedback.

Sporting, quarter-finalists last season for the first time since 1983, fought back to see off Galatasaray 3-1 in Lisbon.

Galatasaray took an early lead through Gonçalo Inacio’s own goal but Geny ​Catamo punished poor defending to equalise in the 27th minute. Luis Suárez converted a 57th-minute penalty to put Sporting ahead and a blistering free kick from Rodrigo Zalazar six minutes later sealed the win.

Sports.title: Cole Palmer powers Chelsea to comeback win over Leeds in nine-goal epic
Sports.content:
Where’s the fun in doing it the easy way? Chelsea remain chaotic at the back but can drag their opponents into horrible places. It helps, mind you, to have some assistance from the referee. Jarred Gillett and Cole Palmer? They made for a killer ­combination as Chelsea swerved embarrassment and treated Stamford Bridge to one of life’s rarities: a classic in the third round of the Carabao Cup.

Gillett, a referee who always seems to be guessing when he makes key calls, was the villain as far as Leeds were concerned. They had just gone 2-0 up when Gillett altered the flow of the tie by pointing to the spot after Pep Chavarría made the most of slight contact from Daniel James. The subsequent conversion from Palmer was inevitable and from there so was the comeback from Chelsea, who rattled through four goals in 12 minutes before eventually reaching the last 16 by winning 6-3.

It made little sense. It could have gone down as Xabi Alonso’s first ­misjudgment as Chelsea’s manager. The Carabao Cup is important given the Spaniard’s side are not in Europe, but his rotation almost backfired. Chelsea were shambolic after making nine changes – the 16-year-old debutant Reggie Watson was overrun in midfield while Estêvão Willian and Jamie Gittens struggled in attack – and Alonso was in emergency mode when he made a quadruple change at half-time.

“I take responsibility,” Alonso said. “No player is to blame. It’s the ­decisions we took. When you don’t have this time to work with them, it’s difficult to compete at this level. I need to take my own blame for the things that happen. I need to be able to help them better. They are not responsible. After you need to react and think what’s better for the team.”

Quick Guide Championship: Ten-man West Brom win at Derby to go top Show West Bromwich Albion held on for a memorable 1-0 victory over Derby at Pride Park, after playing for more than an hour with 10 men. Aune Heggebø's early goal proved enough to take the Baggies top of the table, despite Brayann Pereira being dismissed on his debut after collecting two first-half yellow cards. Derby had started the stronger, but West Brom swept downfield to score in the 16th minute, Jimmy-Jay Morgan whipping in a low cross from the left which Heggebø [pictured] finished at the near post. The visitors were rocked by the dismissal of Pereira in the 34th minute, as he was shown a second yellow card for a clumsy challenge on Charlie Taylor. The hosts went close just before half-time when David Ozoh flashed a low ball across the six-yard box with no white shirt able to turn it in. Derby should have levelled in the 68th minute but Lars-Jørgen Salvesen headed over from Joe Ward’s cross. Late on, Nat Phillips made a great clearance after a late goalmouth scramble, summing up a performance full of grit and resolve. James Morrison's side move above West Ham to top the Championship table with 13 points from six games. Either Charlton or QPR could have joined them on 13 points, but the sides played out a stalemate at the Valley. Derby, meanwhile, slipped into the bottom three with their fourth defeat in six games. Norwich moved up to ninth in the table as they edged past visitors Birmingham 2-1 to make it three wins in four league games. Oscar Schwartau's screamer opened the scoring, the young Dane lashing an unstoppable right-footed drive past James Beadle from 25 yards out. Papa Diallo's first goal for the Canaries doubled their advantage before the break, as the Senegal winger sidefooted home from Andre Brooks' cross. Carlos Vicente pulled a goal back for the visitors, but wasted a glorious chance to equalise near the end as Chris Davies’ men suffered their first league defeat this season. Press Association Photograph: Morgan Harlow/Getty Images Europe Was this helpful? Thank you for your feedback.

Equally Alonso can take credit for responding. His moves were decisive. Reece James offered security after replacing Watson and Pedro Neto scored after coming on for Malo Gusto, who could barely complete a pass during a wretched first half. Leeds, beaten at this stage for the 14th time in 18 years, were overwhelmed once their lead was halved. Morgan Rogers and Palmer were devastating after replacing Estêvão and Gittens. Rogers had a hand in four goals and Palmer, who scored twice, seemed affronted by the notion of Leeds going through.

It finished as another thrilling attacking display from Chelsea, who have scored 16 goals in Alonso’s first five games. There are flaws to fix at the other end, though. Leeds also experimented, Daniel Farke making eight changes, but controlled the first half. They led when the Bosnia and Herzegovina centre-back Tarik Muharemovic, signed from Sassuolo last summer, headed Harry Wilson’s corner past Mike Penders in the 23rd minute.

Chelsea have already conceded 10 goals in all competitions. Leeds could have doubled their lead through Sean Longstaff. Valentín Barco and ­Watson, son of the former Wigan ­midfielder Ben Watson, were second best in midfield.

Leeds were on their way when Barco lost possession three minutes into the second half. Ethan Ampadu charged past Rogers and found Lukas Nmecha, who teed up Brenden ­Aaronson to make it 2-0.

skip past newsletter promotion Free newsletter | Every weekday Sign up to Football Daily Kick off your evenings with the Guardian's take on the world of football Enter your email Sign up after newsletter promotion

View image in fullscreen Pedro Neto fires home Chelsea’s third goal at Stamford Bridge. Photograph: Adam Davy/PA

Chelsea needed a lift. Chavarría crossed from the left and went to ground. Gillett whistled and Palmer scored with 53 minutes played. “He gave out of nothing a penalty where it wasn’t even a chance for them,” Farke said. “A quality player scores and the body language of the Chelsea players was different.”

Palmer was in his element, equalising in the 55th minute after Rogers laid the ball off for his pal to stroke a casual finish past Michael Zetterer from 20 yards. Chelsea were rampant and led on the hour, Palmer and Rogers combining for Neto to finish well. Leeds looked dizzy. They readied the changes but Danny Welbeck made it 4-2 with a sharp turn and finish in the 65th minute.

Leeds kept fighting. Dominic Calvert-Lewin came on and pulled one back to remind Alonso of Chelsea’s defensive weaknesses. Chelsea responded, Rogers crossing for Barco to score his first goal for the club. The sixth followed, Barco’s mis-hit shot diverted in by Welbeck. “A crazy nuts game,” Farke said. That’s been the way for Chelsea under Alonso.

Sports.title: Scottish Premiership: Miovski hits last-gasp Rangers winner and Celtic keep 100% record
Sports.content:
A dramatic last-gasp strike from substitute Bojan Miovski gave Rangers a 1-0 Premiership win over St Mirren at Ibrox.

Back in the technical area after a two-game touchline suspension, Derek McInnes watched St Mirren’s Australian goalkeeper Jacob Chapman keep the home side at bay in the first half with a string of saves, albeit helped by some poor finishing.

Craig McLeish’s side, who lost 5-1 at Ibrox in the Premier Sports Cup last month, grew in confidence after the break and Fraser Taylor missed a great chance while the frustrated home support returned to the state of agitation which characterised the start of the season.

However, in the final seconds of normal time, Miovski, on for Djeidi Gassama, pounced in the box to grab the winner to make it four victories in a row.

Summer signing Mika Baur notched his first goal for Celtic as the Scottish champions maintained their perfect start to their title defence with a 1-0 victory away to St Johnstone.

View image in fullscreen Celtic’s Mika Baur scored his first Celtic goal at McDiarmid Park. Photograph: Steve Welsh/PA

The German midfielder struck from close range early in the second half after the debutant Hoops keeper Sam Johnstone had produced a stunning first-half save to deny Saints midfielder Joel Cotterill.

It was a night when the Celtic head coach, Martin O’Neill, was able to demonstrate the depth of his squad before Sunday’s Old Firm meeting away to Rangers in the Premier Sports Cup, with key players such as Camilo Duran, Benjamin Nygren and Kieran Tierney on the bench and defender Cameron Carter-Vickers given the evening off.

Although far from their convincing best, the Hoops did enough to close out a sixth consecutive league victory this term and their 13th in a row in total stretching back to the closing weeks of last season.

Sports.title: Infantino installs loyalist to oversee Caribbean as he splits Fifa management
Sports.content:
Gianni Infantino has separated Fifa’s management of the Caribbean countries from the rest of Concacaf in a move widely regarded by his opponents as an attempt to split the alliance to remove him from office.

Concacaf covers North and Central America as well as the Caribbean and was previously managed as one bloc. But the Guardian has learned that the former Switzerland midfielder Gelson Fernandes, an Infantino loyalist, has been appointed as the director of member associations for the Caribbean, in addition to his position looking after Fifa’s African members.

Fernandes, who played for Manchester City, Leicester and eight other clubs, joined Fifa in 2022 as director of member associations for Africa and was promoted two years later to become deputy chief members associations officer globally.

The 40-year-old works closely with Fifa’s chief members associations officer, Elkhan Mammadov, a close ally of Infantino described by many national associations as the president’s key enforcer.

Fernandes has replaced Jair Bertoni as Fifa’s liaison with the 21 Caribbean-based members, with the national associations and Concacaf informed of the change last week without consultation.

In a statement Fifa confirmed the appointment, which it said was designed to support Infantino’s vision of making the sport truly global.

“Fifa can confirm that Gelson Fernandes has taken on responsibility for the Caribbean region, in addition to his current role as regional director Africa,” it said. “With his extensive experience at Fifa and strong knowledge of football development programmes, Gelson will lead the regional team and will work closely with the member associations across the Caribbean to further support the development of football in their respective countries, following the Fifa president’s vision: making football truly global.”

Concacaf is attempting with Uefa and the Asian Football Confederation (AFC) to oust Infantino. Sources at several member associations in Europe and North America regard the change as an attempt to split the Concacaf vote before March’s presidential election, with one characterising it as “an administrative war” against its president, Victor Montagliani.

The Canadian is viewed by many in Uefa as the most credible candidate to beat Infantino, although Montagliani has yet to decide whether to stand and is committed to seeking re-election as Concacaf’s president.

Infantino has stepped up his re-election campaign in the aftermath of the World Cup sell-off scandal, ignoring a written request from Montagliani to stay away from a meeting of the Caribbean Football Union (CFU) in the Dominican Republic last month.

As revealed by the Guardian, Infantino used the CFU meeting to announce approval for numerous Fifa-funded development projects for the region worth millions of dollars in what some observers described as an attempt to lobby for votes.

Mexico has split from Concacaf by announcing its support for Infantino, and losing the backing of the Caribbean would be a significant setback for those pushing to remove Infantino.

skip past newsletter promotion Free newsletter | Fortnightly Sign up to The Hotspot A new fortnightly newsletter covering the intersection of sport and the climate crisis Enter your email Sign up after newsletter promotion

There have been some early signs that Infantino’s tactics are paying off, with the president of the Jamaican federation, Michael Ricketts, this week backing the status quo and comparing Uefa to spoiled children.

“Infantino might have made a mistake, but the intentions were to help Caribbean countries or help smaller countries,” Rickets told the Jamaica Observer. “Can you imagine Jamaica getting $40m to invest in football? Can you imagine the difference that would make in four or five years?

“I am not supporting Uefa because I think that they always want to be in opposition and always want to oppose. It doesn’t matter who is president, they are going to have issues. It doesn’t matter how well the president does, they are going to have issues and I think that Uefa is behaving like a set of spoilt kids.”

Uefa’s 55 members are believed to be united but the strength of the AFC alliance is unclear, with Qatar, Saudi Arabia and the United Arab Emirates having defied the confederation by endorsing Infantino.

Infantino last weekend reaffirmed his intention to seek re-election for a fourth term. The deadline for other candidates seeking to stand is 18 November.

Sports.title: Manchester United vs Sabah LIVE commentary: Red Devils handed unique date for Champions League opener
Sports.content:
Manchester United make their long-awaited Champions League return with an unusual Thursday night clash this evening.

The Red Devils are appearing in UEFA's premier club competition for the first time since 2023.



3 United begin their Champions League campaign against Sabah on Thursday night Credit: Getty

It follows their third place finish in the Premier League last term, having failed to qualify for Europe at all the season prior.

Michael Carrick's side kick-off their league phase campaign at home to Azeri champions Sabah.

The match has been scheduled for Thursday night, a rarity in the Champions League.



Fixtures are typically played on Tuesdays and Wednesdays, with Thursdays reserved for the Europa League and Conference League.

Sports.title: ‘Like I volleyed his cat’ – Nathan Jones calls out ‘arrogant’ official in classic interview
Sports.content:
‘Like I volleyed his cat’ – Nathan Jones calls out ‘arrogant’ official in classic interview

Charlton boss Nathan Jones has been left mystified by a linesman's 'arrogance' following a controversial decision in Wednesday's 0-0 draw with QPR.

The Welshman has declared that Bhupinder Gill 'looked at me like I'd volleyed his cat' after the flag went up to wipe out Tyreece Campbell's goal.

4 Campbell was denied his fifth goal of the season as Charlton were held at home against QPR Credit: Getty

In a game of few chances for the Addicks, the hosts thought they had taken the lead in the 39th minute at The Valley.

What was the controversial decision in Charlton's draw with QPR?

A wonderful driving run and pass from ex-Tottenham midfielder Oliver Skipp split the QPR defence.

Jamaica international Campbell latched onto the ball, where he calmly slotted home past the onrushing Pierce Charles with a first-time finish from outside the box.

But his celebrations were immediately cut short as Gill had raised his flag just moments before the 22-year-old released his strike.

With no VAR in the EFL, replays have proven inconclusive to determine whether Campbell was robbed of his fifth strike of the season.

However, Jones has been left in no uncertain terms that his side were on the wrong end of an incorrect call.

And he failed to hold back in his view of Gill, as he declared he was met with utter disdain when protesting the major talking point.

What did Nathan Jones say about the linesman?

Speaking to Sky Sports following the full-time whistle, Jones fumed: "We scored the only goal of the game.

"And once again... I'm sick of it, honestly, I'm sick of it, on the weekend [during 4-0 defeat at Stoke], I had to put up with a performance from an individual that was... I want to use adjectives, but I can't because I'll get in trouble - that was beyond the realm of beliefs.

"And tonight, he [Gill] had one decision to make and he gave offside.

4 Jones believes Campbell was onside after he was played through on goal by Skipp Credit: Sky Sports

4 But the Jamaica international was controversially adjudged to be offside

"They were giving offsides willy-nilly, we had one [offside] in the second half which wasn't.

"And the goal is a great goal, it's a great ball, it's a great counter-attack.

"It is onside and it has cost us three points, that's cost us three points.

"And then the arrogance of the linesman is mental, because he's like [scrunching his face while shaking his head].

"He's looking at me as if I've just volleyed his cat.

"He's looking at me as if I have done something and going, 'Nah.'

4 Jones was left fuming with assistant referee Gill as he slammed his 'arrogance' Credit: Sky Sports

"And he's made the biggest error of the night and he's cost us the game and that is the Championship because the Championship is brutal.

"These are good sides, we're competing with monsters, but we stick at it, the honesty, the defensive resilience we've shown, our keeper [Arthur Okonkwo] has had to make one save."

Jones then signed off his rant by saying: "I'm proud of my team, it was a tough game against a really good team.

"But we have been cost by one individual."

How have Charlton fared this season?

The stalemate lifts Charlton up to fifth spot in the table, with the London outfit picking up 11 points from their opening six games.

Having failed to win any of their last three matches, they will be looking to return to winning ways against Portsmouth on Saturday.

Sports.title: How to follow Liverpool vs Fulham: Arbeloa returns to Anfield aiming to succeed in test Gerrard failed twice

How to follow Liverpool vs Fulham: Arbeloa returns to Anfield aiming to succeed in test Gerrard failed twice

Former Liverpool defender Alvaro Arbeloa returns to Anfield this weekend as his Fulham side take on the Reds.

Arbeloa played 98 games for Liverpool from 2007 to 2009, featuring 66 times in the Premier League during that stint.



3 Arbeloa is returning to Anfield as a manager after spending two years there as a player Credit: Getty

He's now going to be back on Merseyside, hoping to come out on top against his old side and pick up a much-needed win.

Fulham have lost their first three games in the Premier League this season, with boss Arbeloa still waiting on three points.

That has the Cottagers sitting 19th in the table heading into this clash, so they will be desperate for a victory.



History, however, doesn't give Arbeloa much chance of glory on his return to Anfield this Saturday afternoon.

Three previous Liverpool players have taken on the club as a manager in the Premier League, but none of them have won.



Paul Ince was in charge of Blackburn in 2008 when his side were beaten by the Reds, while Mauricio Pellegrino lost twice to his old club when managing Southampton in 2017/18.

And most recently, club icon Steven Gerrard lost both of his meetings with Liverpool with Aston Villa in the 2021/22 campaign.



Can Arbeloa put an end to that losing streak? He'll hope to do so, particularly to Fulham's dismal start to the season.

How to follow Liverpool vs Fulham

Sports.title: Mauricio Pochettino reveals Tottenham mistake in talks to reappoint him as manager
Sports.content:
Mauricio Pochettino reveals Tottenham mistake in talks to reappoint him as manager

Mauricio Pochettino has revealed he will always be open to returning to Tottenham Hotspur as manager.

However, the club have only ever made contact with him when he is unavailable.

3 Pochettino has revealed timing has prevented him from returning to Spurs Credit: Getty

Pochettino spent five years in charge of the north London outfit between 2014 and 2019.

During that time, he achieved five successive top five finishes including two third places and a runner-up spot in the Premier League.

Spurs' second place finish under Pochettino in 2017 remains their highest league position for 63 years.

He also guided the club to the final of both the League Cup and the Champions League.

Of his 293 matches as manager across all competitions, Pochettino collected 160 wins at a win rate of 54.6 per cent.

Only three permanent managers in the club's 144-year history have had a higher win percentage.

Why did Pochettino not return to Spurs?

However, Pochettino was denied a return to the club last season due to his existing commitments with the USA.

Having been appointed in 2024, he was preparing for their World Cup campaign when Spurs approached him to come back to the club.

Pochettino explained: "If I were free, I would have gone back to Tottenham.

"Even in the Championship. Whatever the division. Another club, no, but Tottenham, yes, of course. It’s the only club I’m always open to help."

3 Pochettino oversaw three successive top three finishes and a run to the Champions League final with Spurs Credit: Getty

Spurs avoided relegation from the Premier League by just two points last season thanks to a final day victory over Everton.

Roberto De Zerbi was appointed as manager in April, securing survival by picking up 11 points from the final seven matches.

It could have easily been Pochettino in charge for the relegation run-in, though, with the Argentinian adding: "The problem was the timings were never the best.

"When I was free, I never received a contact and then when I was working, I received a contact and then I couldn’t make the decision to come back.

"It was a little bit unlucky. Maybe one day the stars will align and it will happen."

Pochettino's post-Spurs career

Pochettino instead went on to lead the USA to the last 16 of this summer's World Cup, which they co-hosted with Canada and Mexico.

3 Pochettino signed a new four-year deal with the USA national team in August Credit: Getty

Although his deal had expired at the end of the tournament, he signed a new contract last month.

The 54-year-old will now remain in charge through to the 2030 World Cup.

Prior to moving into international management, Pochettino has had spells with both Paris Saint-Germain and Chelsea since his Spurs exit.

He spent 18 months as PSG boss following his appointment in January 2021.

During that time, Pochettino won both the Ligue 1 title and the French Cup with his former side.

Meanwhile, his Chelsea tenure lasted just one season, with the Blues finishing sixth in the 2023/24 season.

Pochettino made headlines on Thursday for saying Tottenham should be awarded Chelsea's 2016/17 Premier League title.

Sunderland vs Arsenal LIVE commentary: Bruno Guimaraes set for hostile debut in enemy territory

Arsenal head to Sunderland this weekend aiming to continue their blistering start to the season.

The reigning Premier League champions have made a flawless start to the season with three consecutive victories to kickstart their title defence.

3 Mikel Arteta's side are already looking like the team to beat this season Credit: Getty

Arsenal kicked off the season with a convincing 3-0 win over Coventry before a hard-fought 1-0 victory at Aston Villa.

Last time out, the Gunners came from behind to see off Xabi Alonso’s Chelsea in arguably their toughest test of the season.

Next up, is a trip to the Stadium of Light where Mikel Arteta’s side could only manage a 2-2 draw last season.

Sunderland quickly bounced back from their opening day defeat at Ipswich by picking up four points in their last two matches.

A 1-0 win over Fulham preceded Saturday’s 1-1 draw at Brentford and boss Regis Le Bris will be plotting a huge upset in this weekend’s clash.

Sunderland vs Arsenal team news

The Gunners boss could hand £75million summer signing Bruno Guimaraes his first Premier League start following his return from injury.

Arsenal will be without the injured William Saliba (back) while there are doubts over Cristhian Mosquera and Jurrien Timber.

Bukayo Saka and Kai Havertz are expected to start on Wearside after their early-season goalcoring exploits.

Sunderland, meanwhile, will be without Habib Diarra who has been sidelined by a thigh injury.

Le Bris can count on key trio Enzo Le Fée, Nilson Angulo and Granit Xhaka against Arteta’s men.

3 Arteta was delighted with his side's gutsy win over Chelsea Credit: Getty

Arteta lauds his side’s character

Arsenal fell behind to Morgan Rogers’ early strike against Chelsea on Sunday but showed their champion credentials to claim all three points.

“It was an exceptional performance,” Arteta said.

“I enjoyed every minute from beginning to end, and the beginning was tough.

"But the team responded in a spectacular way – the conviction, the determination, the quality. It was beautiful. It was a fascinating game.

“I think it’s an indication for us of how we are capable of ­performing at an even higher level than last ­season.

It depends on how we maintain and sustain that desire, that humbleness, and continue every day to try to find a better version of myself and the team.

"We still have a lot to grow and a lot to offer. This is the ambition of the team.”

Sports.title: Mauricio Pochettino branded a ‘loser’ for saying Tottenham should get Chelsea’s 2017 title
Sports.content:
Mauricio Pochettino branded a ‘loser’ for saying Tottenham should get Chelsea’s 2017 title

Mauricio Pochettino has been called out for a 'loser mentality' after claiming Tottenham deserve to be awarded Chelsea's 2016/17 Premier League title.

The Argentine's Spurs side finished runner-up to Antonio Conte's Blues that season, seven points adrift of the eventual champions.

4 Conte won the Premier League and FA Cup during his two-year spell in charge of Chelsea between 2016-2018 Credit: Getty

However, Pochettino believes Chelsea should be stripped of the trophy, having admitted to breaking the rules.

The current Blues administration self-reported widespread financial irregularities that occurred during the Roman Abramovich era.

This included millions in secret payments to agents, helping to secure a number of players that starred in the 2016/17 title-winning season - including Eden Hazard, Willian and David Luiz.

Chelsea escaped with a £10million fine and a suspended transfer ban, avoiding any sporting sanctions.

But Pochettino, who also managed the Blues in recent years, argues the 2016/17 title should be retrospectively given to his Tottenham side by default.

“I have no doubt and I’m not scared to say the truth," the current USA manager said.

“The Chelsea fans will be upset with me because I’m saying this.

“It’s not me complaining. It’s the truth.

“If they admitted they broke the rules, the Premier League title was for the second best team.

“Otherwise, what is being promoted and incentivised is to break the rules. They admitted, so that’s it. The title should be for the team that was second.”

4 Hazard was the best player in the Premier League during the 2016/17 season Credit: Getty

4 But should it have been Harry Kane lifting the trophy?

Pochettino added: “If we were at Tottenham and broke the rules I’d admit the same and say ‘look, we don’t deserve the title because we broke the rules’.

“You don’t have some clubs playing with the offside laws and VAR and another side without them. That’s impossible.

“No. For everyone it needs to be the same rules and the same capacity to create the best team.

“I’m not saying they didn’t play well.

“That was Conte, the coach was great, and everything.”

'Loser mentality'

talkSPORT pundit and Chelsea fan Rory Jennings ripped into Pochettino for his outlandish claim on Wednesday night's Sports Bar.

4 Pochettino's men came up seven points short in the 2016/17 season and never truly threatened Chelsea for the title Credit: AFP or licensors

"Pochettino is demonstrating loser mentality," Jennings told co-host and Tottenham fan Majestic. "That's what this is.

"Give us something on a technicality that we didn't really earn. You don't want that. You're better than this."

Veteran talkSPORT host and former Tottenham striker Alan Brazil also dismissed Pochettino's calls for the record to be rewritten.

"It doesn't work like that. It's gone now," Brazil said on Thursday morning's Breakfast Show.
